# Who Really Ruled Travancore? The Fascinating Mystery of Padmanabhaswamy Temple

![Image 2: Padmanabhaswamy Temple gopuram in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, associated with the Travancore royal family and Lord Padmanabha](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/wp-content/webp-express/webp-images/uploads/2026/08/Padmanabhaswamy-Temple-gopuram.jpg.webp)

The towering gopuram of Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, a historic landmark closely connected with the Travancore royal family and Lord Padmanabha.

Every now and then, history presents us with a story so unusual that it sounds almost fictional.

A powerful king builds a successful kingdom.

He wins battles.

Expands his territory.

Strengthens his administration.

And then, at the height of his power, he does something entirely unexpected.

He gives the kingdom away.

Not to another ruler.

Not to a conquering army.

Not to a family member.

He gives it to a deity.

At first glance, it sounds impossible.

Yet that is exactly what happened in eighteenth-century Travancore.

The king was Marthanda Varma.

The deity was Lord Padmanabha.

And the place at the heart of this remarkable story was the Padmanabhaswamy Temple in present-day Thiruvananthapuram.

Most people encounter the temple through stories about its enormous treasure vaults. Those stories are certainly fascinating, and we will come to them shortly.

But if you ask me, the treasure is not the most interesting mystery here.

The real mystery is this:

How did a deity become the ruler of an entire kingdom?

And why did generations of kings willingly serve as the deity’s representatives rather than claim the throne for themselves?

That is the sort of question Detective Col. Zoro would find impossible to ignore.

**[Detective Col. Zoro Book 5 – Padmanabhaswamy Temple](link_9)**

* * *

## **Quick Answer: Why Is Padmanabhaswamy Temple Famous?**

Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram is famous for three reasons.

First, it is one of the most important Vishnu temples in India.

Second, it is associated with the Travancore royal family and King Marthanda Varma’s decision to dedicate his kingdom to Lord Padmanabha.

Third, it became internationally famous after vast treasures were discovered in several temple vaults during modern investigations.

Together, these elements make it one of India’s most fascinating historical and cultural landmarks.

* * *

## **The Temple Before the Kingdom**

One of the easiest mistakes to make when learning about Padmanabhaswamy Temple is to assume that the temple became important because of Travancore.

The reality is almost the opposite.

The temple was already ancient long before Travancore emerged as a major kingdom.

References to the site appear in historical records, traditions and literary works dating back many centuries. The deity worshipped here, Lord Vishnu reclining on the serpent Anantha, gave the city its very name.

Thiruvananthapuram literally means:

“The City of Lord Anantha.”

Which means the temple was not simply located within the kingdom.

In many ways, the kingdom grew around the temple.

And that distinction becomes important later.

Because when Marthanda Varma made one of the most extraordinary decisions in Indian history, he was building upon traditions that already ran deep.

* * *

## **The King Who Changed Everything**

By the early eighteenth century, Marthanda Varma had transformed Travancore into one of the strongest kingdoms in southern India.

He defeated rivals.

Expanded the state’s territory.

Strengthened administration.

Modernised the military.

By almost any measure, he was a successful ruler.

Which makes what happened next all the more remarkable.

In 1750, Marthanda Varma performed what became known as the **Thrippadidanam**.

In a symbolic act of dedication, he offered his kingdom to Lord Padmanabha.

From that point onward, the deity was regarded as the true ruler of Travancore.

The kings who followed did not describe themselves as sovereign monarchs.

Instead, they adopted the title:

**Padmanabha Dasa**

Servant of Lord Padmanabha.

Think about that for a moment.

Most rulers throughout history sought to increase their personal authority.

Marthanda Varma voluntarily placed himself beneath the deity he worshipped.

That alone makes this one of the most unusual political stories in Indian history.

* * *

## **The Kingdom with a Divine Ruler**

This is where children usually start asking questions.

If Lord Padmanabha was the ruler, who actually governed the kingdom?

The answer is both simple and fascinating.

The royal family continued administering Travancore.

Laws were made.

Armies were maintained.

Taxes were collected.

The machinery of government continued functioning.

But symbolically, everything was done in the name of Lord Padmanabha.

The kings ruled as custodians rather than owners.

The distinction may seem subtle.

Yet it shaped Travancore’s identity for generations.

And it remains one of the most distinctive features of the kingdom’s history.

* * *

## **The Mystery Beneath the Temple**

Of course, no discussion of Padmanabhaswamy Temple is complete without mentioning the treasure.

This is the part of the story that captures headlines.

For decades, stories circulated about sealed vaults hidden beneath the temple.

Many people assumed the stories were exaggerated.

Then investigations revealed that they were not.

Inside several vaults were astonishing quantities of gold, jewels, coins, ornaments and ceremonial objects accumulated over centuries.

The discoveries attracted international attention.

Suddenly, one of India’s most important temples became one of the most talked-about historical sites in the world.

Yet even here, the treasure is only part of the story.

Because every treasure raises questions.

Who donated these objects?

Over what period?

How were they preserved?

What do they tell us about trade, wealth and devotion in earlier centuries?

The gold may attract attention.

The questions are what make history interesting.

* * *

## **The Case of the Locked Vault**

No article about Padmanabhaswamy Temple would be complete without mentioning Vault B.

Unlike several other vaults that were examined, this particular chamber remains unopened.

Naturally, this has inspired endless speculation.

Legends.

Rumours.

Conspiracy theories.

Wild guesses.

In other words, exactly the sort of thing that would attract Detective Col. Zoro.

The reality is that much about the vault remains uncertain.

And uncertainty has a way of encouraging the imagination.

Sometimes the mysteries we cannot solve become the ones we remember most.

* * *

## **The Clues in the Case**

[![Image 3: Detective Col. Zoro Book 5 Mystery of the Secret Chamber inspired by the history and mysteries of Padmanabhaswamy Temple](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Zoro-5-01.png.webp)](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/product/detective-col-zoro-book-5-mystery-of-the-secret-chamber/ [link_9])
### **THE PADMANABHASWAMY MYSTERY**

Inside are several clues.

*   An ancient temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
*   A city named after the deity.
*   A powerful king.
*   A kingdom offered to a god.
*   Generations of rulers calling themselves servants.
*   Hidden vaults.
*   Extraordinary treasure.
*   An unopened chamber.

Now comes the detective’s question.

Which clue do you think is the most surprising?

For me, it is still the king giving away his kingdom.

Not because it created a mystery.

Because it created a story unlike almost any other in history.

* * *

## **Visit the Temple and Let the Questions Begin**

Some historical sites impress visitors with their size.

Others with their age.

Padmanabhaswamy Temple does something slightly different.

It impresses visitors with the stories it contains.

A king who surrendered a throne.

A deity who became a ruler.

Treasures hidden for centuries.

Questions that remain unanswered.

The moment children hear those stories, they start asking questions.

And that is exactly where learning begins.

* * *

## **Continue the Adventure**

# **FAQ**

## **Why is Padmanabhaswamy Temple famous?**

The temple is famous for its religious significance, its connection to the Travancore royal family and the enormous treasures discovered in its vaults.

## **Who was Marthanda Varma?**

Marthanda Varma was the ruler of Travancore who dedicated his kingdom to Lord Padmanabha in 1750.

## **Why did the kings of Travancore call themselves Padmanabha Dasa?**

After the kingdom was dedicated to Lord Padmanabha, the rulers considered themselves servants of the deity rather than sovereign monarchs.

## **What is the treasure of Padmanabhaswamy Temple?**

The treasure consists of gold, jewels, coins and ceremonial objects accumulated over centuries through donations and royal patronage.

## **What is Vault B?**

Vault B is one of the temple’s sealed chambers and remains unopened, contributing to the mystery surrounding the temple.

# History

![Image 7: Parashuraman](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/03/2018031985.jpg)

Thiruananthapuram, the jewel in the emerald necklace that Kerala is for the Indian sub-continent, must surely have been a “must see” destination for ages, long before National Geographic Traveller classified it as one. Surely long before Sage Parasurama , according to local legend, threw his divine battle axe from Kanyakumari to Gokarnam to wrest Kerala, God’s own land, from the Varuna the sea god; before the times of Mahabali the democratic and justruler of this wonderful land who was sent down to the netherworld through deceit. It doesnt take any flights of fancy to imagine that this land fired the imaginations of intrepid travellers and explorers like Columbus, Vasco da Gama, Marco Polo, Fa Hien, and quite possibly, countless others from the pages of history, recorded or not.

![Image 8: King Marthanda Varma](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/06/2018062617.jpg)

Thiruvananthapuram, or Trivandrum, as it was conveniently re-christened by the English, is the southern-most district and Thiruvananthapuram city is the district headquarters as well as the State capital of Kerala. Thiru Anantha Puram, or the city of the Holy Anantha, is named after Ananthan, the cosmic serpent with a thousand heads, on whose coils Lord Mahavishnu reclines. This iconic representation is the chief deity in the Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple. The temple was built by King Marthanda Varma of the Travancore Royal family when, in 1745, he shifted the Travancore capital from Padmanabhapuram in the south (today in the neighbouring State of Tamil Nadu) to Thiruvananthapuramand started reigning as ‘Padmanabha Dasa’, the servant and representative of Lord Padmanabha–perhaps a nobler variant of the ‘Divine Right Theory’ that the West is familiar with . The vast temple complex, with its tall ‘Gopuram’ decorated with detailed carvings reflected in the huge temple tank, is today a centre of attraction for the pious, the tourist and the merely curious.

![Image 9: Sree Padmanabha Swamy](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/06/2018062640.jpg)

Thiruvananthapuram, built on seven hills, has today growninto a sprawling metropolis; but thankfully the city still retains her past glory and charm, and in spite of the frenetic pace of modern life, perhaps it is the most sedate of the big cities of the State. The people too have retained their friendliness and hospitality, and communicating in English, Hindi or Tamil is as easy as it is in the native Malayalam, whether one is talking to a retired professor or to the man in the street. But be prepared for a ‘dose’ of highly individualistic observations though– a hallmark of the Malayali that has enabled him to adapt and to survive the Tsunamis of alien cultures and ideas, and all things ‘modern’. # History

![Image 7: Parashuraman](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/03/2018031985.jpg)

Thiruananthapuram, the jewel in the emerald necklace that Kerala is for the Indian sub-continent, must surely have been a “must see” destination for ages, long before National Geographic Traveller classified it as one. Surely long before Sage Parasurama , according to local legend, threw his divine battle axe from Kanyakumari to Gokarnam to wrest Kerala, God’s own land, from the Varuna the sea god; before the times of Mahabali the democratic and justruler of this wonderful land who was sent down to the netherworld through deceit. It doesnt take any flights of fancy to imagine that this land fired the imaginations of intrepid travellers and explorers like Columbus, Vasco da Gama, Marco Polo, Fa Hien, and quite possibly, countless others from the pages of history, recorded or not.

![Image 8: King Marthanda Varma](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/06/2018062617.jpg)

Thiruvananthapuram, or Trivandrum, as it was conveniently re-christened by the English, is the southern-most district and Thiruvananthapuram city is the district headquarters as well as the State capital of Kerala. Thiru Anantha Puram, or the city of the Holy Anantha, is named after Ananthan, the cosmic serpent with a thousand heads, on whose coils Lord Mahavishnu reclines. This iconic representation is the chief deity in the Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple. The temple was built by King Marthanda Varma of the Travancore Royal family when, in 1745, he shifted the Travancore capital from Padmanabhapuram in the south (today in the neighbouring State of Tamil Nadu) to Thiruvananthapuramand started reigning as ‘Padmanabha Dasa’, the servant and representative of Lord Padmanabha–perhaps a nobler variant of the ‘Divine Right Theory’ that the West is familiar with . The vast temple complex, with its tall ‘Gopuram’ decorated with detailed carvings reflected in the huge temple tank, is today a centre of attraction for the pious, the tourist and the merely curious.

![Image 9: Sree Padmanabha Swamy](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/06/2018062640.jpg)

Thiruvananthapuram, built on seven hills, has today growninto a sprawling metropolis; but thankfully the city still retains her past glory and charm, and in spite of the frenetic pace of modern life, perhaps it is the most sedate of the big cities of the State. The people too have retained their friendliness and hospitality, and communicating in English, Hindi or Tamil is as easy as it is in the native Malayalam, whether one is talking to a retired professor or to the man in the street. But be prepared for a ‘dose’ of highly individualistic observations though– a hallmark of the Malayali that has enabled him to adapt and to survive the Tsunamis of alien cultures and ideas, and all things ‘modern’. The old quarter of the city clusters in and around the East Fort, a protected landmark that dates back to the Royal days. # Fatehpur Sikri and the Mystery of Vijaypur Sikri

![Image 2: Fatehpur Sikri historical complex near Agra illustrating the mystery of Vijaypur Sikri and the site's possible pre-Mughal past](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/wp-content/webp-express/webp-images/uploads/2026/08/fatehpur-sikri-vijaypur-sikri-mystery.jpg.webp)

Fatehpur Sikri near Agra, where archaeological evidence and theories surrounding Vijaypur Sikri suggest the site's history may stretch back well before Akbar's Mughal capital.

Fatehpur Sikri, near Agra, is one of India’s most famous historical cities.

Ask most people who built it and the answer comes instantly: Akbar.

For generations, that has been the accepted story. Akbar chose the site, built a magnificent capital and transformed it into one of the most remarkable cities of medieval India.

Yet history is rarely as simple as it first appears.

Archaeologists studying the region have uncovered evidence suggesting that the story of Sikri may begin much earlier than Akbar.

And that possibility changes everything.

In fact, it is such a fascinating mystery that it forms the historical backdrop of [_**The Petha and the Missing Brigadier**_](link_9), one of the most intriguing adventures in the Detective Col. Zoro series. Rather than presenting history as a collection of settled facts, the story invites young readers to investigate a question that historians themselves continue to explore.

## **A City Older Than We Think?**

Long before Akbar chose Sikri as his capital, the location already appears to have been important.

Historical references to Sikri predate the Mughal era.

The region is associated with events connected to Rana Sanga and the campaigns that preceded the Battle of Khanwa in 1527.

This immediately raises an interesting question.

If Sikri existed before Akbar, what exactly was there?

A village?

A fortified settlement?

A regional centre?

Or something much larger?

## **Enter Bir Chhabili Tila**

One of the most important pieces of this puzzle comes from Bir Chhabili Tila.

Archaeological investigations in and around the mound have revealed evidence of earlier habitation layers beneath the Mughal city.

Pottery, structural remains and artefacts from different historical periods suggest that the region witnessed human activity long before Akbar arrived.

This does not necessarily mean that the entire Fatehpur Sikri we see today predates the Mughals.

It does suggest, however, that the story of the site is far older than many people realise.

## **The Mystery of Vijaypur Sikri**

This is where the discussion becomes truly fascinating.

Some historians and researchers have proposed that Fatehpur Sikri may have evolved from an earlier settlement associated with Vijaypur Sikri.

The idea remains debated.

Not every scholar agrees.

Not every claim has been conclusively proven.

But that is precisely what makes the topic so compelling.

History is not always about certainty.

Sometimes it is about following evidence wherever it leads.

And the evidence surrounding Sikri continues to raise important questions.

## **Did Akbar Build Fatehpur Sikri?**

The answer depends on what we mean by “build.”

There is little doubt that Akbar built the magnificent Mughal capital that attracts visitors today.

The Buland Darwaza.

The Diwan-i-Khas.

The imperial palaces.

These are undeniably associated with Akbar’s vision.

But archaeology suggests he may not have been building on an empty landscape.

Instead, he may have inherited a location with a much longer history.

Seen this way, recent discoveries do not diminish Akbar’s achievement.

They enrich our understanding of it.

## **Why This Matters**

Whenever I think about historical discoveries like these, I find myself wondering whether we sometimes teach history the wrong way.

Children are often taught history as if every question already has an answer.

But real history is an investigation.

Historians gather evidence.

Archaeologists uncover clues.

Researchers test theories.

New discoveries challenge old assumptions.

In many ways, they work like detectives.

That is why the mystery of Fatehpur Sikri is so valuable.

It shows children that learning history is not about memorising facts.

It is about asking questions.

## **A Lesson in Critical Thinking**

The debate surrounding Vijaypur Sikri teaches children something important.

Evidence matters.

Assumptions should be questioned.

And sometimes the most interesting discoveries emerge when we look beyond accepted narratives.

This is one of the reasons the [**Detective Col. Zoro series**](link_1) resonates so strongly with young readers.

The stories encourage children to investigate, analyse and think independently rather than simply accept conclusions at face value.

## **Bringing History Alive Through Storytelling**

Archaeological reports are fascinating.

For most children, however, they are not exactly bedtime reading.

Stories bridge that gap.

They transform evidence into adventure.

They transform historical questions into mysteries.

And they transform learning into discovery.

That is exactly what happens in [_**The Petha and the Missing Brigadier**_](link_9).

As Col. Zoro follows clues through Agra and Fatehpur Sikri, readers encounter archaeology, competing interpretations and historical investigation in a way that feels exciting rather than academic.

## **Key Takeaway**

The most important question is not whether every theory about Vijaypur Sikri is ultimately proven correct.

The important question is this:

What happens when we discover that history may be more complicated than we once believed?

That moment of curiosity is where real learning begins.

## **Continue the Investigation**

If your child enjoys mysteries, history and asking difficult questions, [_**The Petha and the Missing Brigadier**_](link_9) offers a fascinating introduction to one of India’s most intriguing historical puzzles.

[**Explore the Detective Col. Zoro Series**](link_1)

## **Final Thoughts**

The story of Fatehpur Sikri is ultimately a story about curiosity.

It reminds us that famous places often have forgotten histories.

That accepted narratives can evolve.

And that every archaeological discovery has the potential to change how we understand the past.

Whether future discoveries strengthen the case for Vijaypur Sikri or point historians in entirely new directions, one thing remains certain.

The mystery itself is worth exploring.

For parents looking to nurture curiosity, critical thinking and a love of history, books such as **[_The Petha and the Missing Brigadier_](link_9)**provide a wonderfully engaging gateway into the process of historical investigation.

Because history is not merely something we inherit.

It is something we continue to discover.

[**Order The Petha and the Missing Brigadier**](link_9)

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

### **Was Fatehpur Sikri built by Akbar?**

Akbar built the famous Mughal capital that visitors see today, but archaeological evidence suggests the site may have been occupied long before his reign.

### **What is Vijaypur Sikri?**

Vijaypur Sikri refers to theories and interpretations that associate the Fatehpur Sikri region with an earlier settlement predating the Mughal era.

### **What is Bir Chhabili Tila?**

Bir Chhabili Tila is an archaeological mound near Fatehpur Sikri where excavations have revealed evidence of earlier habitation layers.

### **Why is Fatehpur Sikri important?**

Fatehpur Sikri is one of India’s most significant historical sites and continues to generate debate about the origins and development of the region.

### **What can children learn from The Petha and the Missing Brigadier?**

The book introduces children to archaeology, historical investigation and critical thinking through an entertaining mystery adventure.

# Martand Sun Temple: The Magnificent Wonder That Refused to Be Forgotten

![Image 2: The ruins of Martand Sun Temple at sunrise, with the Kashmir Valley stretching into the distance behind it.](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/wp-content/webp-express/webp-images/uploads/2026/08/Martand-Sun-Temple-at-sunrise-1024x471.jpg.webp)

Martand Sun Temple: The Magnificent Wonder That Refused to Be Forgotten

There are some historical sites that impress you because they are complete.

The Taj Mahal is one.

The Brihadeeswara Temple is another.

You stand before them and admire what survives.

Martand Sun Temple creates a very different feeling.

The first thing that strikes most visitors is not what is there.

It is what is missing.

Broken columns rise from the ground. Fragments of walls stand against the backdrop of the Kashmir Valley. Empty spaces hint at halls, carvings and structures that no longer exist. Even someone with no knowledge of history can tell immediately that this place was once extraordinary.

And that is where the questions begin.

Who built it?

Why was it built here?

How magnificent was it in its prime?

And perhaps most intriguingly of all, what happened to it?

Because Martand is not simply a story about a temple.

It is a story about ambition, beauty, loss and memory.

In many ways, it feels exactly like a Detective Col. Zoro mystery.

Not because nobody knows anything about it.

But because the ruins constantly remind us that there is still so much left to understand.

If your child enjoys mysteries set against India’s monuments and historical sites, Martand is one of those places that sparks curiosity almost immediately.

**[Detective Col. Zoro Book 4 – Martand Sun Temple](link_9)**

* * *

## **Quick Answer: Why Is Martand Sun Temple Famous?**

Martand Sun Temple is an ancient Hindu temple dedicated to Surya, the Sun God, located in Kashmir.

Built during the 8th century CE by King Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty, it is widely regarded as one of the finest examples of ancient Indian temple architecture.

Today, it is famous not only for its beauty and historical importance but also because much of the temple survives only as ruins, making it one of India’s most evocative and intriguing historical sites.

* * *

## **A Temple Built to Match the Landscape**

One of the things photographs struggle to capture about Martand is its setting.

The temple sits on a plateau overlooking the Kashmir Valley, and there is a moment when most visitors realise that the builders knew exactly what they were doing. This was not simply a convenient piece of land on which to construct a temple. The location feels chosen.

The valley stretches out below. Mountains frame the horizon. The sky seems unusually vast.

Even today, standing among the ruins, it is difficult not to pause for a moment and simply look.

King Lalitaditya Muktapida, who commissioned the temple in the eighth century, was responsible for creating one of the most remarkable monuments in ancient India. Scholars often point out the blend of architectural influences visible in the structure, but what strikes many visitors first is something simpler.

Scale.

Even in ruins, Martand feels grand.

You find yourself imagining what the complex must have looked like when its courtyards were intact, its carvings complete and its walls standing at their full height.

The imagination does a great deal of work at Martand.

Perhaps that is one reason the site remains so memorable.

* * *

## **The King Behind the Temple**

Every great monument begins with an idea.

In this case, the idea belonged to Lalitaditya Muktapida, one of the most powerful rulers of the Karkota dynasty.

Historical accounts describe him as an ambitious king whose influence extended far beyond Kashmir. During his reign, the kingdom flourished, and Martand became one of its most impressive achievements.

The temple was dedicated to Surya, the Sun God, but it was also something more.

It was a statement.

A declaration of confidence, prosperity and artistic ambition.

Even today, more than a thousand years later, the surviving ruins continue to communicate that sense of grandeur.

The builders may be long gone, but their confidence still lingers in stone.

* * *

## **The Architecture That Still Amazes Historians**

One of the reasons Martand occupies such an important place in Indian architectural history is that it does not fit neatly into a single category.

The temple reflects influences from Gandharan, Gupta and Kashmiri traditions, creating a style that feels distinctively its own.

At its centre stood the main shrine. Around it stretched a large courtyard surrounded by smaller cells and impressive colonnades.

Visitors today often find themselves trying to reconstruct the monument in their minds.

What did the carvings look like?

How did sunlight move through the complex during the day?

What ceremonies took place here?

How many people worked on its construction?

The ruins do not answer these questions directly.

Instead, they invite us to keep asking them.

* * *

## **When History Takes a Difficult Turn**

Every historical site has moments of triumph.

Some also have moments of tragedy.

Martand’s story includes both.

At some point after centuries of standing proudly over the Kashmir Valley, the temple suffered extensive destruction. Historical accounts often connect this to the reign of Sultan Sikandar in the late fourteenth and early fifteenth centuries, although historians continue discussing the details and sources surrounding the event.

What is not disputed is the outcome.

The magnificent temple was reduced to ruins.

Whenever I visit historical sites like Martand, I find myself wondering about the people who witnessed these changes.

Did they imagine that future generations would still be talking about the monument centuries later?

Could they have imagined that visitors from across India would continue coming here simply to stand among the remains and reflect on what once existed?

History rarely provides answers to such questions.

But it certainly encourages us to ask them.

* * *

## **The Case of the Missing Temple**

One of the reasons Martand feels so perfectly suited to Detective Col. Zoro is that the mystery is hiding in plain sight.

Unlike Dwarka, we are not searching for a city beneath the sea.

Unlike Ajanta, we are not rediscovering caves hidden by forests.

The evidence is right in front of us.

The question is how to interpret it.

Imagine arriving at Martand with no prior knowledge of the site.

What would the ruins tell you?

Would you recognise that this was once a place of immense importance?

Would you be able to estimate its size?

Would you wonder why it was damaged?

Would you ask who built it?

Children are often surprisingly good at this exercise.

They notice details adults overlook.

And before long, they find themselves doing exactly what historians do.

They start asking questions.

That spirit of investigation sits at the heart of the Detective Col. Zoro series.

****[Detective Col. Zoro Book 4 – Martand Sun Temple](link_9)****

* * *

## **The Clues in the Case**

Imagine Col. Zoro handing you a file marked:

### **THE MARTAND MYSTERY**

Inside are a handful of clues.

A powerful king commissions an extraordinary temple.

The monument becomes one of Kashmir’s architectural masterpieces.

Centuries pass.

Political and cultural changes reshape the region.

The temple suffers extensive damage.

The ruins survive.

Future generations continue asking questions.

Now comes the detective’s challenge.

Which part of the story do you think matters most?

The construction?

The destruction?

Or the fact that the monument was remembered at all?

History often focuses on what was lost.

Martand also reminds us to think about what survived.

* * *

## **Visit Martand and Let History Do the Talking**

Some monuments require long explanations.

Martand is not one of them.

The site has a way of speaking for itself.

Children do not need to know every historical detail before arriving.

The ruins take care of that.

They notice the surviving columns.

They look across the valley.

They realise the scale of the structure.

And almost inevitably, they start asking questions.

What happened here?

Who built this?

Why is it broken?

Could it ever be rebuilt?

That curiosity is worth far more than memorising dates.

Because curiosity transforms history from information into discovery.

And discovery is what children remember.

# **FAQ**

## **Why is Martand Sun Temple famous?**

Martand Sun Temple is famous for its remarkable architecture, historical significance and dramatic ruins overlooking the Kashmir Valley.

## **Who built Martand Sun Temple?**

The temple was built in the 8th century CE by King Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty.

## **Why is Martand Sun Temple in ruins?**

Historical accounts attribute its destruction to later political and religious conflicts, although historians continue discussing specific details and sources.

## **What deity was worshipped at Martand Sun Temple?**

The temple was dedicated to Surya, the Sun God.

## **Can families visit Martand Sun Temple today?**

Yes. The ruins remain one of Kashmir’s most important historical and architectural sites.

Markdown Content:
Log in

![Image 1: Muse](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/brand/muse-logo.svg)
# Muse, AI that gets it done for you Muse[Video 1](https://l.facebook.com/videos/avatars/hatch_connecting.mp4)[Video 2](https://l.facebook.com/videos/avatars/hatch_working.mp4), AI that gets it done for you sorts your email books reservations shops for you saves you money manages calendars builds fitness plans gets it done for you sorts your email![Image 2](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-envelope.webp)books reservations![Image 3](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-airplane.webp)shops for you![Image 4](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-cart.webp)saves you money![Image 5](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-piggybank.webp)manages calendars![Image 6](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-calendar.webp)builds fitness plans![Image 7](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/b-01.webp)gets it done for you

# Log in or create an account

Mobile number or email(required) 

You may receive SMS notifications from us by using your mobile number. [Learn more](https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/31983416211257755/)

Continue

[Learn more](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://muse.ai/&h=AUDBdWsOkzpWRdkF_MfYKU1CZsm20fbyay-Gd0KyWqxezdEjuiIaS-YHu7qeRxDr7pNZPv5MW3UJs4GqrsaPWalj8XtlImFe5SdLvvY9_45du9Las0l088EG12-3dej0trISkOCHFJKOaA#landing-introduction-video-title)

## Built around your whole life

Give Muse a goal or task and it handles the rest, from saving money and improving your health to smart shopping and helping you strengthen your relationships.

![Image 8: The Muse app icon](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/placeholders/sizzle.png)

### Every Muse user shares their own computer in the cloud with their Muse.

Muse Secure VM is a persistent, isolated Linux computer with a full browser that you and your agent can use to complete tasks, allowing you to intervene at any point. It's your computer and your browser, with the storage, CPU, and memory to handle real work.

![Image 9: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/browser.webp)![Image 10: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/browser-dark.webp)

### Designed around the way you already communicate

Chat with your agent in the same way you message with other people, using the Muse app on mobile, Mac, or directly in WhatsApp. There's no learning curve, just tell Muse what you want to get done.

![Image 11: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/messaging.webp)![Image 12: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/messaging-dark.webp)

### Stay in control of what your agent does

Approve actions your agent takes on your behalf before they happen, like sending emails and making purchases. See a complete audit trail of everything your agent has done (and what it's planning to do).

![Image 13: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/approvals.webp)![Image 14: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/approvals-dark.webp)

### Your data is kept secure and private

Save your logins to a secure credential store Muse can't see, with 1Password integration coming soon. When shopping, a one-time card number is generated at checkout so your real card stays hidden from the merchant and your agent. Eligible purchases are covered by [Link's purchase protections](https://link.com/protections), a first for AI agents, and your conversations are not shared with Meta's ad systems.

![Image 15: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/secure-storage.webp)![Image 16: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/secure-storage-dark.webp)

### Proactively helps with your goals and suggests ideas

Muse helps you stay on top of things, takes tasks and projects off your plate, and turns long-term goals into real progress. It learns from conversations, reflects on what matters and gets sharper, coming back with ideas built around what you actually need, ready to act on them under your direction.

![Image 17: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/goals.webp)![Image 18: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/goals-dark.webp)

### Connects to your apps and builds its own tools

Connect the apps you use daily, like email, calendar, and Instagram. You decide what your agent can see and what it can do. If a task needs a tool that doesn't exist, your agent builds it for you.

![Image 19: Connected app, messaging, media, cloud, calendar, and automation tiles](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/connectors.webp)

## Get the most out of your Muse

A guided tour of Muse, from setting a first goal to seeing it through.

![Image 20: Product designer presenting a guided tour of Muse](https://l.facebook.com/images/hatch/landing/product-walkthrough-cover.png)

## Learn more about Muse

Explore the choices behind Muse and how it is built to deserve your trust.

### [How We Designed Muse When Muse works, it feels like magic. These are the product choices that make the experience possible.](https://introducing.muse.ai/)### [How We Built Safety Into Muse Muse is built for privacy, safety, and security. Learn how these principles shape every part of the product.](https://security.muse.ai/)### [Muse for Business Meet the AI agent that works for your small business and keeps jobs moving between your decisions.](https://l.facebook.com/business)

## Ready to try Muse?

# Nalanda University and the Bakhtiyarpur Paradox

![Image 2: Nalanda University ruins in Bihar representing ancient Indian education and India’s educational heritage](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/wp-content/webp-express/webp-images/uploads/2026/08/Indian-educational-heritage.jpg.webp)

The ruins of Nalanda University in Bihar, a powerful reminder of India’s ancient educational heritage and one of the world’s most renowned historic centres of learning.

If you visit the ruins of Nalanda University today, there is a good chance your journey will take you through a railway station called Bakhtiyarpur.

At first glance, the name means little to most travellers.

Yet history gives it a peculiar significance.

Bakhtiyarpur is named after Bakhtiyar Khilji, the military commander widely associated with the destruction of Nalanda, one of the greatest centres of learning the world has ever known.

The irony is difficult to ignore.

One of humanity’s most extraordinary universities lies a short distance away.

The railway station many visitors pass through bears the name of the man believed to have played a central role in its destruction.

History rarely produces paradoxes quite like that.

It is precisely the sort of historical mystery that makes children stop and ask questions. In fact, the story is so compelling that it forms the backdrop of **[_The Cheese Chase and the Lost Library_](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/product/detective-col-zoro-book-7-quest-for-the-greatest-treasure/),** one of the most fascinating adventures in the Detective Col. Zoro series. Rather than presenting Nalanda as a collection of dates and facts, the story encourages young readers to investigate one of the greatest educational institutions in human history.

## **What Made Nalanda University So Extraordinary?**

Whenever we think about universities, we tend to imagine lecture halls, libraries and students pursuing degrees.

Nalanda had all of those elements.

The remarkable thing is that it had them more than a thousand years ago.

Founded around the fifth century CE, Nalanda attracted scholars from across Asia. Students travelled from regions corresponding to modern-day China, Korea, Tibet, Mongolia and Southeast Asia to study there.

The university housed thousands of students and teachers.

It possessed vast libraries.

It encouraged intellectual debate.

It attracted some of the greatest minds of its age.

In many ways, Nalanda resembled a modern international university centuries before such institutions became common.

That alone would make it historically significant.

The scale of its achievement makes it extraordinary.

## **Centuries Ahead of Its Time**

One of the reasons Nalanda continues to fascinate historians is that it feels surprisingly modern.

Admission was selective.

Students travelled internationally to study there.

Ideas moved across borders.

Knowledge was preserved, debated and expanded.

Subjects extended far beyond religion.

Scholars studied philosophy, astronomy, mathematics, medicine, logic, linguistics and literature.

In an age when much of the world was still organised around local centres of learning, Nalanda functioned as a global intellectual hub.

That is why describing it merely as a university feels inadequate.

It was closer to a knowledge ecosystem.

A place where ideas from different cultures met, interacted and evolved.

When children encounter Nalanda for the first time, they are often surprised by how advanced it was. That sense of wonder sits at the heart of [_**The Cheese Chase and the Lost Library**_](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/product/detective-col-zoro-book-7-quest-for-the-greatest-treasure/), where Detective Col. Zoro and his companions explore clues connected to one of history’s most remarkable centres of learning.

## **The Tragedy of Nalanda**

Every great institution has a story.

Nalanda’s story contains one of history’s greatest tragedies.

By the late twelfth century, military campaigns led by Bakhtiyar Khilji swept through parts of Bihar.

Historical accounts associate these invasions with the destruction of major Buddhist centres, including Nalanda.

The university never recovered.

The famous libraries disappeared.

Centuries of accumulated knowledge were lost.

The scholars dispersed.

The institution that had once attracted students from across Asia gradually faded into history.

What makes the story particularly heartbreaking is not merely that buildings were destroyed.

Buildings can be rebuilt.

Knowledge, once lost, is far harder to recover.

## **Was Nalanda Destroyed Out of Fear?**

The exact motivations behind Bakhtiyar Khilji’s actions remain debated.

Historians can often establish what happened more confidently than why it happened.

Yet it is difficult not to reflect on the symbolism.

A military commander seeking power destroyed an institution dedicated to knowledge.

One represented force.

The other represented learning.

One sought conquest.

The other pursued understanding.

Whether fear, hostility, indifference or strategic calculation drove the destruction, the result was the same.

One of humanity’s greatest centres of education disappeared.

That loss continues to resonate more than eight centuries later.

## **The Bakhtiyarpur Paradox**

And this brings us back to the railway station.

Every year, visitors travel to Nalanda through Bakhtiyarpur.

The contrast is striking.

The place remembered for learning survives in ruins.

The name remembered in connection with its destruction survives on signboards, railway announcements and maps.

History has a curious sense of humour.

The paradox forces us to ask uncomfortable questions about memory.

Who do we choose to remember?

What do we choose to celebrate?

And how should societies preserve the stories that matter most?

These are not merely historical questions.

They are detective questions.

They require us to investigate evidence, challenge assumptions and think critically about the past. That approach runs through the entire **[Detective Col. Zoro series](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/product-category/books/)**, where history becomes far more interesting when it is explored as a mystery rather than memorised as a list of facts.

## **Why Nalanda Matters Today**

It is tempting to view Nalanda as a relic of a distant past.

That would be a mistake.

Nalanda reminds us that India has a long and distinguished educational heritage.

Long before modern universities emerged across much of the world, scholars were travelling thousands of kilometres to study in Bihar.

Long before globalisation became a buzzword, Nalanda was attracting international students.

Long before modern research institutions, intellectual communities were gathering there to exchange ideas.

The story challenges the assumption that advanced education is a recent phenomenon.

In many respects, Nalanda was centuries ahead of its time.

This is one of the reasons [_**The Cheese Chase and the Lost Library**_](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/product/detective-col-zoro-book-7-quest-for-the-greatest-treasure/) works so well as an introduction to Nalanda for younger readers. Instead of focusing only on dates and historical events, it captures the wonder of a university that was shaping minds from across Asia long before most of the world had anything comparable.

## **Why Children Should Learn About Nalanda**

Whenever I think about Nalanda, I find myself wondering how many children know its story.

Most know about kings.

Many know about battles.

Far fewer know about universities.

Yet institutions like Nalanda shaped history just as profoundly as armies did.

Learning about Nalanda teaches children something important.

Civilisations are remembered not only for the wars they fought.

They are remembered for the knowledge they created.

The books they preserved.

The questions they asked.

The ideas they shared.

That is why stories like [_**The Cheese Chase and the Lost Library**_](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/product/detective-col-zoro-book-7-quest-for-the-greatest-treasure/) matter. They introduce children to India’s educational heritage through adventure, curiosity and investigation, making a complex historical story accessible without sacrificing its depth.

## **Exploring Nalanda Through Detective Col. Zoro**

One of the challenges of teaching history is that the most fascinating subjects are often buried beneath dates, terminology and textbook summaries.

Nalanda deserves better than that.

Its story is filled with international travellers, legendary libraries, intellectual debate, mystery and loss. It contains all the ingredients of a compelling adventure.

That is precisely what makes it such a natural setting for Detective Col. Zoro.

In [_**The Cheese Chase and the Lost Library**_](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/product/detective-col-zoro-book-7-quest-for-the-greatest-treasure/), young readers encounter Nalanda not as a forgotten ruin, but as a living mystery. As Col. Zoro follows clues connected to a lost library, children begin to appreciate why Nalanda mattered, how advanced it was and why its destruction remains one of history’s greatest cultural tragedies.

The result is something rare.

A story that entertains while simultaneously inspiring curiosity about India’s past.

## **Final Thoughts**

The story of Nalanda is ultimately a story about the power of knowledge.

Empires rose and fell.

Kings came and went.

Armies marched across continents.

Yet centuries later, people still speak about Nalanda.

Not because it conquered territory.

But because it expanded human understanding.

Perhaps that is the greatest lesson of all.

Power can destroy a university.

It cannot erase what that university represents.

And perhaps that is why the ruins of Nalanda continue to inspire awe even today.

Because long after the conquerors have disappeared, the pursuit of knowledge remains.

For parents looking to introduce children to this extraordinary chapter of Indian history, [_**The Cheese Chase and the Lost Library**_](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/product/detective-col-zoro-book-7-quest-for-the-greatest-treasure/) offers an engaging gateway into the world of Nalanda, its scholars, its mysteries and its enduring legacy.

### **What was Nalanda University?**

Nalanda University was one of the world’s oldest and most influential centres of learning, located in present-day Bihar, India.

### **Who destroyed Nalanda University?**

Historical accounts associate the destruction of Nalanda with the military campaigns of Bakhtiyar Khilji in the late twelfth century.

### **Why was Nalanda important?**

Nalanda attracted scholars from across Asia and taught subjects including philosophy, mathematics, astronomy, medicine and logic.

### **Was Nalanda really centuries ahead of its time?**

Yes. Nalanda functioned as an international residential university with thousands of students and scholars long before such institutions became common elsewhere.

### **How can children learn about Nalanda?**

Books such as _The Cheese Chase and the Lost Library_ introduce young readers to Nalanda’s history through engaging stories, mysteries and adventures.

Zoro** as he uncovers hidden secrets, dangerous motives, and a mystery far greater than anyone expected.

Specially designed for curious young readers, this engaging illustrated mystery novella blends **detective storytelling, Indian history, ancient architecture, cultural heritage, and critical thinking** into one unforgettable reading experience. Zoro and his companions uncover strange clues connected to the magnificent **Martand Sun Temple**, one of India’s most fascinating yet lesser-known historical landmarks.

As secrets begin to surface, hidden motives emerge, and danger intensifies, Col. Zoro realizes that the mystery surrounding the temple is far larger and more dangerous than expected. Through careful observation, courage, and sharp detective instincts, he must uncover the truth before history itself is threatened.

With suspense growing at every turn, hidden truths waiting to be uncovered, and clues scattered throughout the journey, **Col. The story inspires children to stay curious while understanding the importance of protecting India’s historical treasures.

# About District

Thiruvananthapuram also known as Trivandrum, is the capital and the largest city of the Indian state of Kerala. The city has a population of 957,730 inhabitants and a metropolitan population of 1.68 million. Thiruvananthapuram is a major Information Technology hub in India, and contributes 55% of Kerala’s software exports as of 2015.Thiruvananthapuram is located on the west coast of India near the extreme south of the mainland. Referred by Mahatma Gandhi as the “Evergreen city of India”,the city is characterised by its undulating terrain of low coastal hills.The city is classified as a Tier-II city by the government of India.

## Boundaries

Thiruvananthapuram district is situated between north latitudes 8º 17′ and 8º 54′ and east longitudes 76º 41′ and 77º 17′.  
 The southern most extremity, ‘Parasala’, is 56 kms away from Kanyakumari, the “land’s end of India”. The district stretches along the shores of the Arabian sea for a distance of 78 kms.

# Places of Interest

![Image 7: padmanabha swamy temple](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/04/2018040474-300x180.jpg)
**SREE PADMANABHA SWAMY TEMPLE**

The origin of the Temple of Sree Padmanabhaswamy is lost in antiquity. It is not possible to determine with any exactitude, from any reliable historical documents or other sources as to when and by whom the original idol of Sree Padmanabhaswamy was consecrated. The Temple has references in Epics and Puranas. Srimad Bhagavatha says that Balarama visited this Temple, bathed in Padmatheertham and made several offerings. Nammalwar, 9th century poet and one among the 12 Vaishnavite saints of the Alvar tradition, has composed ten hymns in praise of Lord Padmanabha. Some well known scholars, writers and historians, like the late Dr. L.A.Ravi Varma of Travancore, have expressed the view that this Temple was established on the first day of Kali Yuga (which is over 5000 years ago). The legends of the Temple are handed down through the centuries. One such legend which finds a place in the old palm leaf records of the Temple, as also in the famous grantha entitled “Ananthasayana Mahatmya”, mentions that it was consecrated by a Tulu Brahmin hermit named Divakara Muni. On the 950th year of Kali Yuga a reinstallation of the idol was done. In the 960th Kali year King Kotha Marthandan built the Abhisravana Mandapam.The principal deity Vishnu is enshrined in the “Anantha Shayanam” posture, the eternal yogic sleep on the serpent Adisheshan.Sree Padmanabhaswamy is the tutelary deity of the royal family of Travancore. The titular Maharaja of Travancore Moolam Thirunal Rama Varma is the trustee of the temple. The name of the city of Thiruvananthapuram in Malayalam translates to “The City of Lord Ananta”,referring to the deity of Padmanabhaswamy Temple.

For more details please visit :[http://www.sreepadmanabhaswamytemple.org](http://www.sreepadmanabhaswamytemple.org/)

* * *

![Image 8: Zoo](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/04/2018040467-300x180.jpg)
**MUSEUM AND ZOO IN THIRUVANANTHAPURAM**

Thiruvananthapuram Museums & Zoo owe its orgin to the joint efforts of Mr. J.A. Brown, former Director of Thiruvananthapuram Observatory, and General Cullen, a former British Resident. A committee was formed in 1855 with the Maharaja of Travancore as patron, General Cullen as President, the Elaya Raja as Vice President and Mr. Allen Brown as Secretary of the Committee and the Director of Museum. This Museum was thrown open to the public in September 1857. But the Museum by itself could not attract the people much, and therefore a Zoo and a Park known as public gardens were started in 1859. # Did Krishna’s Dwarka Really Exist? The Mystery Beneath the Sea

![Image 2: Underwater ruins near Dwarka, Gujarat, showing submerged stone structures associated with the ancient city linked to Lord Krishna.](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/wp-content/webp-express/webp-images/uploads/2026/07/Underwater-ruins-near-Dwarka.jpg.webp)

Submerged stone ruins near Dwarka, Gujarat, where archaeological discoveries have inspired ongoing research into India's ancient maritime history and the legendary city of Lord Krishna.

History occasionally produces mysteries so extraordinary that they sound as though they belong in a Detective Col. Zoro adventure.

An ancient city described in texts thousands of years old.

A city associated with Krishna.

A city said to have disappeared beneath the sea.

For centuries, most people placed Dwarka firmly in the realm of mythology and tradition. It was a story. A powerful story. An enduring story. But a story nonetheless.

Then archaeologists started finding things underwater.

And suddenly the conversation became much more interesting.

Because finding traces of an ancient settlement beneath the sea has a way of making people sit up and pay attention.

It certainly caught mine.

The first time I came across the underwater discoveries off the coast of modern Dwarka, I found myself doing exactly what I suspect many parents and children do when they encounter a good mystery.

I started asking questions.

What exactly was found?

How old was it?

Could it really be connected to the Dwarka described in ancient texts?

How much of the story is supported by evidence?

And how much remains uncertain?

Those questions eventually led me down one of the most fascinating historical rabbit holes I have explored in recent years.

Not because the answers are simple.

Because they aren’t.

* * *

## **Quick Answer: Did Dwarka Really Exist?**

Archaeological discoveries off the coast of modern Dwarka have revealed submerged structures, stone anchors and evidence of ancient coastal settlements.

Many researchers believe these discoveries suggest that ancient urban settlements once existed in the area.

Whether the remains belong to the exact Dwarka described in texts such as the Mahabharata remains debated. However, the discoveries have convinced many historians and archaeologists that the traditions surrounding an ancient city near modern Dwarka may have been based on a real place.

* * *

## **Why Dwarka Refuses to Go Away**

What makes the story of Dwarka so unusual is that it refuses to stay neatly in any one category.

It is not quite mythology.

It is not quite archaeology.

It is not quite history.

And it is certainly not a mystery that has been completely solved.

Most ancient cities leave behind ruins that archaeologists can walk through, excavate and analyse. Dwarka presents a rather different challenge.

According to tradition, the city disappeared beneath the sea.

If that were true, where would one even begin looking?

For centuries, the answer was simple.

You didn’t.

The story survived in texts, traditions and memory.

Then marine archaeologists started exploring the waters off the Gujarat coast.

And suddenly a question that had once seemed impossible became entirely reasonable:

Could there be more to the story than we realised?

That question is what makes Dwarka such a compelling mystery.

Not because we have all the answers.

Because we don’t.

* * *

## **The First Clue: What the Ancient Texts Tell Us**

Every investigation begins somewhere.

In the case of Dwarka, it begins with ancient texts.

The Mahabharata, Harivamsha and Bhagavata Purana describe Dwarka as a magnificent coastal city associated with Krishna.

The descriptions are surprisingly detailed.

We read of fortifications, harbours, prosperity and maritime connections. We also encounter one of the most intriguing elements of the story: the tradition that the city was eventually reclaimed by the sea.

Now, ancient texts are not archaeological evidence.

But they do provide something extremely valuable.

They provide clues.

Many historical discoveries begin with clues preserved in literature, oral traditions and historical accounts. Archaeologists rarely start with answers. They start with leads.

And Dwarka provided a very intriguing lead indeed.

* * *

## **The Second Clue: What Archaeologists Found Beneath the Sea**

This is where the story becomes particularly fascinating.

Marine archaeological surveys conducted off the coast of Dwarka revealed a variety of submerged structures and artefacts.

Stone anchors.

Structural remains.

Evidence suggesting maritime activity.

Possible harbour installations.

What makes these discoveries important is not any single object. Archaeology rarely works that way.

Instead, archaeologists look for patterns.

A wall by itself tells us very little.

A wall, anchors, settlement remains and evidence of human activity found together begin telling a story.

Over time, researchers assembled a picture suggesting that ancient settlements once occupied parts of this coastline and that these settlements had significant connections to the sea.

The discoveries did not end the debate.

But they certainly changed it.

The discussion shifted from “Could there have been an ancient settlement here?” to “What exactly have we found?”

That is a very different conversation.

* * *

## **The Third Clue: The Sky**

One of the more surprising aspects of the Dwarka mystery has nothing to do with archaeology at all.

It has to do with astronomy.

Ancient Indian texts contain numerous descriptions of eclipses, planetary positions and celestial events. Some researchers have attempted to analyse these references using modern astronomical software.

The idea is surprisingly straightforward.

If an ancient text describes a specific combination of astronomical events, could those events be used to estimate when the text was describing?

The field is known as archaeoastronomy.

The conclusions remain debated.

Different researchers arrive at different dates.

Not all scholars accept the methodology.

Yet the fact that researchers continue studying these astronomical references tells us something important.

The story is being investigated seriously.

And that, in itself, is fascinating.

* * *

## **The Clues in the Case**

Imagine Detective Col. Zoro handing you a file marked:

### **THE DWARKA MYSTERY**

Inside you find the following clues:

*   Ancient texts describe a coastal city.
*   The city is associated with Krishna.
*   Traditions claim it disappeared beneath the sea.
*   Archaeologists discover submerged structures.
*   Ancient anchors are found nearby.
*   Researchers study astronomical references in ancient texts.
*   Debate continues.

Now comes the detective’s question.

Which clue do you find most convincing?

The answer is less important than the discussion.

Because this is exactly how historical investigations work.

Evidence is collected.

Claims are examined.

Different interpretations are compared.

And conclusions are reached cautiously.

That is also the philosophy behind Detective Col. Zoro.

The books encourage children to approach history as an investigation rather than a collection of facts waiting to be memorised.

**[Detective Col. Zoro Book 2 – Dwarka](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/product/detective-col-zoro-book-2-legend-of-the-drowned-city/)**

* * *

## **If Col. Zoro Investigated Dwarka**

I sometimes wonder what questions Col. Zoro would ask if he found himself standing on the coast of Dwarka.

Would he begin with the archaeological evidence?

Would he compare ancient texts?

Would he investigate the underwater structures?

Or would he start by asking the simplest question of all:

“What can we actually prove?”

That, after all, is the heart of every good mystery.

Separating what we know from what we think we know.

Separating evidence from assumption.

Following the clues wherever they lead.

Which is precisely what makes Dwarka such an enduring story.

* * *

## **Visit Dwarka and Watch the Mystery Come Alive**

One of the remarkable things about this mystery is that families can still visit the place where it unfolds.

The Dwarkadhish Temple continues to attract visitors from across India and beyond.

The Arabian Sea stretches out beyond the city.

And somewhere beneath those waters lies one of the most intriguing archaeological stories in India.

Standing on the shore, it is difficult not to wonder what remains hidden beneath the waves.

And perhaps that is the real appeal of Dwarka.

Not that every question has been answered.

But that some mysteries continue inviting us to ask better questions.

# **FAQ**

## **Did Krishna’s Dwarka really exist?**

Archaeological discoveries near modern Dwarka suggest that ancient settlements existed in the region. Whether these remains correspond exactly to the Dwarka described in ancient texts remains under discussion.

## **What evidence exists for Dwarka?**

Evidence includes submerged structures, stone anchors, archaeological discoveries and literary references from ancient texts.

## **What is archaeoastronomy?**

Archaeoastronomy studies astronomical references in ancient cultures and texts to better understand historical timelines and events.

## **Why is Dwarka important?**

Dwarka sits at the intersection of archaeology, history, astronomy, literature and tradition, making it one of India’s most fascinating historical mysteries.

![Image 7: padmanabha swamy temple](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/04/2018040474-300x180.jpg)
**SREE PADMANABHA SWAMY TEMPLE**

The origin of the Temple of Sree Padmanabhaswamy is lost in antiquity. It is not possible to determine with any exactitude, from any reliable historical documents or other sources as to when and by whom the original idol of Sree Padmanabhaswamy was consecrated. The Temple has references in Epics and Puranas. Srimad Bhagavatha says that Balarama visited this Temple, bathed in Padmatheertham and made several offerings. Nammalwar, 9th century poet and one among the 12 Vaishnavite saints of the Alvar tradition, has composed ten hymns in praise of Lord Padmanabha. Some well known scholars, writers and historians, like the late Dr. L.A.Ravi Varma of Travancore, have expressed the view that this Temple was established on the first day of Kali Yuga (which is over 5000 years ago). The legends of the Temple are handed down through the centuries. One such legend which finds a place in the old palm leaf records of the Temple, as also in the famous grantha entitled “Ananthasayana Mahatmya”, mentions that it was consecrated by a Tulu Brahmin hermit named Divakara Muni. On the 950th year of Kali Yuga a reinstallation of the idol was done. In the 960th Kali year King Kotha Marthandan built the Abhisravana Mandapam.The principal deity Vishnu is enshrined in the “Anantha Shayanam” posture, the eternal yogic sleep on the serpent Adisheshan.Sree Padmanabhaswamy is the tutelary deity of the royal family of Travancore. The titular Maharaja of Travancore Moolam Thirunal Rama Varma is the trustee of the temple. The name of the city of Thiruvananthapuram in Malayalam translates to “The City of Lord Ananta”,referring to the deity of Padmanabhaswamy Temple.

For more details please visit :[http://www.sreepadmanabhaswamytemple.org](http://www.sreepadmanabhaswamytemple.org/)

**MUSEUM AND ZOO IN THIRUVANANTHAPURAM**

Thiruvananthapuram Museums & Zoo owe its orgin to the joint efforts of Mr. J.A. Brown, former Director of Thiruvananthapuram Observatory, and General Cullen, a former British Resident. A committee was formed in 1855 with the Maharaja of Travancore as patron, General Cullen as President, the Elaya Raja as Vice President and Mr. Allen Brown as Secretary of the Committee and the Director of Museum. This Museum was thrown open to the public in September 1857. But the Museum by itself could not attract the people much, and therefore a Zoo and a Park known as public gardens were started in 1859. By 1880, a new building designed by Robert Chisholm, Architect to the Governor of Madras, was constructed and the Museum was shifted to the present architectural beauty The Thiruvananthapuram Zoo and Museums Complex was initially established as to provide a means of recreation for the public. The Thiruvananthapuram Zoo and Museums Complex, situated in 55 acres of land, right in the heart of Thiruvananthapura City Entrance fee for adults is Rs. 20 and children between 5 – 12 years areRs. 5. Camera permit costs Rs. 50/-

Nearest airport:Trivandrum International Airport, about 5 km away

**SREE CHITRA ART GALLERY**

Established in 1935 by the then Maharaja of Travancore, Sree Chithira Thirunal, the Sree Chithra Art Gallery near the Napier Museum displays a rare collection of paintings. Works of acclaimed artists like Raja Ravi Varma, Svetlova and Nicholas Roerich; exquisite works from the Mughal, Rajput and Tanjore schools of art, are on display here. An oriental collection consisting of paintings from China, Japan, Tibet and Bali offers a visual treat and are a tribute to the art and culture of these countries. The collection also includes unique copies of Indian mural paintings from pre-historic times down to the 18th Century.

Visiting Hours:10:00 to 16:45 hrs. It is closed on Mondays & Wednesday forenoons

**MAGIC PLANET THEME PARK TRIVANDRUM**

The Magic Planet located in Thiruvananthapuram which claims to be the world’s first magic themed park is fast emerging as a major tourist spot in Kerala. Envisaged to showcase the wonders of magic and explore its endless possibilities, the doors to this castle of magic have been thrown open to the public.

A multitude of fascinating activities await visitors here. Among the many segments, the ‘Street Magic Venue’ which displays spellbinding performances and tricks such as ‘The Indian Mango Mystery’ and the ‘Indian Basket Trick’ on the streets attract visitors in hordes. Be it the magical session displaying William Shakespeare’s ‘The Tempest’, or the ‘Magic Gallery’ at the History Museum with its rare memorabilia tracing the tale of magic and magicians from the middle ages to the 1950s, or the ‘Circus Castle’ where hypnotic and mesmerising acts are staged, the Magic Planet will enthrall you beyond words.

Apart from these exquisite and magical treats, this enchanting place has a host of other gripping attractions that can charm you forever. Magic Planet is situated at KINFRA Film and Video Park, Kazhakuttam, in the capital city.

**KOVALAM BEACH**

Kovalam is an internationally renowned beach with three adjacent crescent beaches. It has been a favourite haunt of tourists since the 1930s. A massive rocky promontory on the beach has created a beautiful bay of calm waters ideal for sea bathing.

The leisure options at this beach are plenty and diverse. Sunbathing, swimming, herbal body toning massages, special cultural programmes and catamaran cruising are some of them. The tropical sun acts so fast that one can see the faint blush of coppery tan on the skin in a matter of minutes. Life on the beach begins late in the day and carries on well into the night. The beach complex includes a string of budget cottages, Ayurvedic health resorts, convention facilities, shopping zones, swimming pools, Yoga and Ayurvedic massage centres

Accommodation facilities for tourists at Kovalam range from five star hotels to budget hotels and the choice of food available at restaurants and cafeterias range from Continental varieties to South Indian delicacies.

Nearest railway station: Thiruvananthapuram Central, about 16 km

Nearest airport: Trivandrum International Airport, about 10 km

**VARKALA BEACH**

Location: 51 km north of Thiruvananthapuram city in Thiruvananthapuram district and 37 km south of Kollam, south Kerala.

Varkala, a calm and quiet hamlet, lies on the outskirts of Thiruvananthapuram district. It has several tourist attractions that include a beautiful beach, a 2000-year-old Vishnu Temple and the Ashramam – Sivagiri Mutt a little distance from the beach.

The Papanasam Beach (also called as Varkala Beach), which is ten kilometers away from Varkala, is renowned for a natural spring. Which is considered to have medicinal and curative properties. A dip in the holy waters at this beach is believed to purge the body of impurities and the soul of all sins; hence the name ‘Papanasam Beach’.

**VELI TOURIST VILLAGE**

The Veli Tourist Village which lies where the Veli Lake meets the Arabian Sea provides for unique boating and picnicking opportunities. Visitors can hire pedal boats or paddleboats as per their convenience. One can also roam the gardens and have a nice picnic or choose to employ the boats for the entire duration of the trip. The view and feel of the place is extremely unique, considering it is merely 12 kms from the capital city of Thiruvananthapuram. Children are known to have a lot of fun climbing the sculptures here and the speedboat ride across the waters. A separate Children’s Park and Floating Cafe run by Kerala Tourism Development Corporation (KTDC) are added incentives to visit this unique village.

**SANKHUMUGHAM BEACH**

Shankumugham Beach is a beach in Thiruvananthapuram district of Kerala, south India. The vast stretch of white sand and the serene atmosphere, away from the crowd in the city, provide all the ingredients for relaxation and for spending an ideal evening. There is also a “Star Fish Restaurant” with eating kiosks and open-air theatre with car parking facilities. Good food can be enjoyed at the Old Coffee House, just across the beach, which is also a vantage point for enjoying the sunset. Shanghumugham beach is considered as the ‘Arattukadavu’ of Sri Ananthapadmanabhan – The presiding deity of the city. Thousands of Hindus perform ‘Bali Tharpanam’ during special occasions. Shanghu mugham is the prime location for Ganesh Nimarjan at the time of Vinayaka Chathurthi.

**NEYYAR DAM**

Neyyar dam is a gravity dam on the Neyyar River in Thiruvananthapuram district of Kerala, South India, located on the foot of the Western Ghats about 30 km from Thiruvananthapuram.It was established in 1958 and is a popular picnic spot. Lying against the southern low hills of the Western Ghats, Neyyar Dam has a scenic lake.

Neyyar dam is situated at Kallikkad Panchayath of Kattakkada Taluk of Trivandrum district. The peak Agasthya kooodam is very near to Neyyar dam. The dam was built in the land given by an agriculturist known as Karuvachiyil Krishan Panicker, Father of Janaki Thankamma, Maruthummoottil family, and his other family members for irrigation purposes. One canal of Neyyar flows to western districts of Tamil Nadu. The main river Neyyar flows through Kallikkadu, Ottasekharamangalam, Aryancode, Kezharoor, Perumkadavila, Marayamuttom, Neyyattinkara and Poovar and ends at the Arabian Sea.

**PONMUDI HILL STATION**

Ponmudi is a hill station in the Thiruvananthapuram District of Kerala in India. It is located 55.2 km north-east of Trivandrum City at an altitude of 1100 m. Ponmudi peak is a part of the Western Ghats mountain range that runs parallel to the Arabian Sea.

Ponmudi is connected to Trivandrum by a two lane highway (SH2 & SH 45). The last 18km starting from Anapara has scenic views, as it winds through the mountains and tea gardens. The travel along this stretch provides a thrilling experience as drivers and riders have to navigate 22 Hairpin turns. Ponmudi is also a popular spot for backpacking and trekking. The climate is pleasant year-round.ther attractions near Ponmudi include Golden Valley and a number of rivulets and rapids, some even across the road. The lush forest area has tropical vegetation.A variety of wildlife inhabit the hills. The Golden Valley offers vistas of the hills and access to the Kallar River. Flowing though a wilderness area, it has rounded pebbles, cool water, fish, and lush green trees.

Nearest railway station:Thiruvananthapuram, about 61 km away

Nearest airport:Trivandrum International Airport, about 67 km away

**ARUVIKKARA DAM**

Near a beautiful Durga Temple lies a stream where people can be regularly seen feeding fish who pop up close to the shore. Visitors stroll around leisurely the pristine picnic spots. These are some of the visuals one sees at Aruvikkara Dam. Located on the outskirts of Thiruvananthapuram City, whose water supply it is responsible for, Aruvikkara is ideal for a weekend drive from the State capital. The serene Karamana River invites you and a fun filled jaunt is guaranteed on every trip here.

Nearest railway station: Thiruvananthapuram, about 16 km

Nearest airport: Trivandrum International Airport, about 23 km

Latitude: 8.57559, Longitude: 77.025461
