# History

![Image 7: Parashuraman](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/03/2018031985.jpg)

Thiruananthapuram, the jewel in the emerald necklace that Kerala is for the Indian sub-continent, must surely have been a “must see” destination for ages, long before National Geographic Traveller classified it as one. Surely long before Sage Parasurama , according to local legend, threw his divine battle axe from Kanyakumari to Gokarnam to wrest Kerala, God’s own land, from the Varuna the sea god; before the times of Mahabali the democratic and justruler of this wonderful land who was sent down to the netherworld through deceit. It doesnt take any flights of fancy to imagine that this land fired the imaginations of intrepid travellers and explorers like Columbus, Vasco da Gama, Marco Polo, Fa Hien, and quite possibly, countless others from the pages of history, recorded or not.

![Image 8: King Marthanda Varma](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/06/2018062617.jpg)

Thiruvananthapuram, or Trivandrum, as it was conveniently re-christened by the English, is the southern-most district and Thiruvananthapuram city is the district headquarters as well as the State capital of Kerala. Thiru Anantha Puram, or the city of the Holy Anantha, is named after Ananthan, the cosmic serpent with a thousand heads, on whose coils Lord Mahavishnu reclines. This iconic representation is the chief deity in the Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple. The temple was built by King Marthanda Varma of the Travancore Royal family when, in 1745, he shifted the Travancore capital from Padmanabhapuram in the south (today in the neighbouring State of Tamil Nadu) to Thiruvananthapuramand started reigning as ‘Padmanabha Dasa’, the servant and representative of Lord Padmanabha–perhaps a nobler variant of the ‘Divine Right Theory’ that the West is familiar with . The vast temple complex, with its tall ‘Gopuram’ decorated with detailed carvings reflected in the huge temple tank, is today a centre of attraction for the pious, the tourist and the merely curious.

![Image 9: Sree Padmanabha Swamy](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/06/2018062640.jpg)

Thiruvananthapuram, built on seven hills, has today growninto a sprawling metropolis; but thankfully the city still retains her past glory and charm, and in spite of the frenetic pace of modern life, perhaps it is the most sedate of the big cities of the State. The people too have retained their friendliness and hospitality, and communicating in English, Hindi or Tamil is as easy as it is in the native Malayalam, whether one is talking to a retired professor or to the man in the street. But be prepared for a ‘dose’ of highly individualistic observations though– a hallmark of the Malayali that has enabled him to adapt and to survive the Tsunamis of alien cultures and ideas, and all things ‘modern’. The old quarter of the city clusters in and around the East Fort, a protected landmark that dates back to the Royal days. The rightly famous Sri Padmanabhaswamy temple , the Navarathri Mandapam, where the annual musical fest is held as an offering to Saraswati, the Goddess of Learning , Kuthira Malika, a uniquely wonderful example of traditional architecture and the venue of the annual Swathi Thirunal music festival honouring the composer-king of Travancore are the best among the traditional structures that adorn the Fort enclave. The Mahatma Gandhi Road, the chief artery of the city, is lined by traditional mansions that proclaim the grandeur of the times past and modern high-rises that testify to the city’s newfound affluence and a brashly commercial taste –red tile and timber vying with concrete and glass. What perhaps is special about the ambience of Thiruvananthapuram is the wonderful blend of the strongly traditional, the nostalgically Colonial and the outright modern elements, be it in architecture, in food or in the dress and manners of her people. The city’s spirit of ‘live and let live’ is nowhere more evident than at Palayam (the Garrison, the seat of the old Cantonment), where threecentres of worships of three faiths rub shoulders–the ancient Ganapathy Temple (ostensibly built by the Maharajah for the prosperity of the Connemara Market nearby), the Palayam Muslim Mosque (get the correct name) and the Palayam Christian Cathedral (get the correct name) church with its distinctive Gothic tower.

![Image 10: Kadhakali](https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s313fe9d84310e77f13a6d184dbf1232f3/uploads/2018/06/2018062698.jpg)

Blessed with a pleasant climate virtually throughout the year, Thiruvananthapuram city sparkles after the monsoon rains. After the ‘hot’ summers, which thankfully pale in comparison to the ‘hotspots’ of India, the welcome summer showers augur the festival season when Kerala decks herself out, and traditional colours and rhythms and characters straight from the pages of her ancient lore entice the visitor to another world. The festivities are crowned by Onam , the Spring harvest festival, today marked by traditional fare throughout the State, including the spirited race of the picturesque and majestic snake boats , the grand elephant parade, when hordes of caparisoned pachyderms lend an air of fantasy to the setting, and the special presentations of Kathakali , Mohiniyattom , Koodiyattom and other traditional arts of Kerala. etc

### ABOUT DISTRICT

Thiruananthapuram, the jewel in the emerald necklace that Kerala is for the Indian sub-continent, must surely have been a “must see” destination for ages, long before National Geographic Traveller classified it as one.

Thiruvananthapuram, or Trivandrum, as it was conveniently re-christened by the English, is the southern-most district and Thiruvananthapuram city is the district headquarters as well as the State capital of Kerala.

Thiru Anantha Puram, or the city of the Holy Anantha, is named after Ananthan, the cosmic serpent with a thousand heads, on whose coils Lord Mahavishnu reclines. This iconic representation is the chief deity in the Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple.

# Who Really Ruled Travancore? The Fascinating Mystery of Padmanabhaswamy Temple

![Image 2: Padmanabhaswamy Temple gopuram in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, associated with the Travancore royal family and Lord Padmanabha](https://biplobworld.com/zoroverse/wp-content/webp-express/webp-images/uploads/2026/08/Padmanabhaswamy-Temple-gopuram.jpg.webp)

The towering gopuram of Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, a historic landmark closely connected with the Travancore royal family and Lord Padmanabha.

Every now and then, history presents us with a story so unusual that it sounds almost fictional.

A powerful king builds a successful kingdom.

He wins battles.

Expands his territory.

Strengthens his administration.

And then, at the height of his power, he does something entirely unexpected.

He gives the kingdom away.

Not to another ruler.

Not to a conquering army.

Not to a family member.

He gives it to a deity.

At first glance, it sounds impossible.

Yet that is exactly what happened in eighteenth-century Travancore.

The king was Marthanda Varma.

The deity was Lord Padmanabha.

And the place at the heart of this remarkable story was the Padmanabhaswamy Temple in present-day Thiruvananthapuram.

Most people encounter the temple through stories about its enormous treasure vaults. Those stories are certainly fascinating, and we will come to them shortly.

But if you ask me, the treasure is not the most interesting mystery here.

The real mystery is this:

How did a deity become the ruler of an entire kingdom?

And why did generations of kings willingly serve as the deity’s representatives rather than claim the throne for themselves?

That is the sort of question Detective Col. Zoro would find impossible to ignore.

## **Quick Answer: Why Is Padmanabhaswamy Temple Famous?**

Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram is famous for three reasons.

First, it is one of the most important Vishnu temples in India.

Second, it is associated with the Travancore royal family and King Marthanda Varma’s decision to dedicate his kingdom to Lord Padmanabha.

Third, it became internationally famous after vast treasures were discovered in several temple vaults during modern investigations.

Together, these elements make it one of India’s most fascinating historical and cultural landmarks.

* * *

## **The Temple Before the Kingdom**

One of the easiest mistakes to make when learning about Padmanabhaswamy Temple is to assume that the temple became important because of Travancore.

The reality is almost the opposite.

The temple was already ancient long before Travancore emerged as a major kingdom.

References to the site appear in historical records, traditions and literary works dating back many centuries. The deity worshipped here, Lord Vishnu reclining on the serpent Anantha, gave the city its very name.

Thiruvananthapuram literally means:

“The City of Lord Anantha.”

Which means the temple was not simply located within the kingdom.

In many ways, the kingdom grew around the temple.

And that distinction becomes important later.

Because when Marthanda Varma made one of the most extraordinary decisions in Indian history, he was building upon traditions that already ran deep.

* * *

## **The King Who Changed Everything**

By the early eighteenth century, Marthanda Varma had transformed Travancore into one of the strongest kingdoms in southern India.

He defeated rivals.

Expanded the state’s territory.

Strengthened administration.

Modernised the military.

By almost any measure, he was a successful ruler.

Which makes what happened next all the more remarkable.

In 1750, Marthanda Varma performed what became known as the **Thrippadidanam**.

In a symbolic act of dedication, he offered his kingdom to Lord Padmanabha.

From that point onward, the deity was regarded as the true ruler of Travancore.

The kings who followed did not describe themselves as sovereign monarchs.

Instead, they adopted the title:

**Padmanabha Dasa**

Servant of Lord Padmanabha.

Think about that for a moment.

Most rulers throughout history sought to increase their personal authority.

Marthanda Varma voluntarily placed himself beneath the deity he worshipped.

That alone makes this one of the most unusual political stories in Indian history.

* * *

## **The Kingdom with a Divine Ruler**

This is where children usually start asking questions.

If Lord Padmanabha was the ruler, who actually governed the kingdom?

The answer is both simple and fascinating.

The royal family continued administering Travancore.

Laws were made.

Armies were maintained.

Taxes were collected.

The machinery of government continued functioning.

But symbolically, everything was done in the name of Lord Padmanabha.

The kings ruled as custodians rather than owners.

The distinction may seem subtle.

Yet it shaped Travancore’s identity for generations.

And it remains one of the most distinctive features of the kingdom’s history.

* * *

## **The Mystery Beneath the Temple**

Of course, no discussion of Padmanabhaswamy Temple is complete without mentioning the treasure.

This is the part of the story that captures headlines.

For decades, stories circulated about sealed vaults hidden beneath the temple.

Many people assumed the stories were exaggerated.

Then investigations revealed that they were not.

Inside several vaults were astonishing quantities of gold, jewels, coins, ornaments and ceremonial objects accumulated over centuries.

The discoveries attracted international attention.

Suddenly, one of India’s most important temples became one of the most talked-about historical sites in the world.

Yet even here, the treasure is only part of the story.

Because every treasure raises questions.

Who donated these objects?

Over what period?

How were they preserved?

What do they tell us about trade, wealth and devotion in earlier centuries?

The gold may attract attention.

The questions are what make history interesting.

* * *

## **The Case of the Locked Vault**

No article about Padmanabhaswamy Temple would be complete without mentioning Vault B.

Unlike several other vaults that were examined, this particular chamber remains unopened.

Naturally, this has inspired endless speculation.

Legends.

Rumours.

Conspiracy theories.

Wild guesses.

In other words, exactly the sort of thing that would attract Detective Col. Zoro.

The reality is that much about the vault remains uncertain.

And uncertainty has a way of encouraging the imagination.

Sometimes the mysteries we cannot solve become the ones we remember most.

# **FAQ**

## **Why is Padmanabhaswamy Temple famous?**

The temple is famous for its religious significance, its connection to the Travancore royal family and the enormous treasures discovered in its vaults.

## **Who was Marthanda Varma?**

Marthanda Varma was the ruler of Travancore who dedicated his kingdom to Lord Padmanabha in 1750.

## **Why did the kings of Travancore call themselves Padmanabha Dasa?**

After the kingdom was dedicated to Lord Padmanabha, the rulers considered themselves servants of the deity rather than sovereign monarchs.

## **What is the treasure of Padmanabhaswamy Temple?**

The treasure consists of gold, jewels, coins and ceremonial objects accumulated over centuries through donations and royal patronage.

## **What is Vault B?**

Vault B is one of the temple’s sealed chambers and remains unopened, contributing to the mystery surrounding the temple.

# About District

Thiruvananthapuram also known as Trivandrum, is the capital and the largest city of the Indian state of Kerala. The city has a population of 957,730 inhabitants and a metropolitan population of 1.68 million. Thiruvananthapuram is a major Information Technology hub in India, and contributes 55% of Kerala’s software exports as of 2015.Thiruvananthapuram is located on the west coast of India near the extreme south of the mainland. Referred by Mahatma Gandhi as the “Evergreen city of India”,the city is characterised by its undulating terrain of low coastal hills.The city is classified as a Tier-II city by the government of India.

# Thiruvananthapuram Population 2026

Thiruvananthapuram city is governed by Municipal Corporation which comes under [Thiruvananthapuram Metropolitan Region](link_27). The Thiruvananthapuram city is located in Kerala state of India.

Travel Guides & Travelogues

  
 The current estimate population of Thiruvananthapuram city in 2026 is 1,116,000 , while Thiruvananthapuram metro population is estimated at 2,528,000 . The last census was conducted in 2011 and the schedule census for Thiruvananthapuram city in 2021 was postponed due to Covid. The current estimates of Thiruvananthapuram city are based on past growth rate. Once govt conducts census for Thiruvananthapuram city, we will update the same here in 2026. As per provisional reports of Census India, population of Thiruvananthapuram in 2011 is 743,691. Although Thiruvananthapuram city has population of 743,691; its urban / metropolitan population is 1,679,754. 
### Thiruvananthapuram Literacy Rate and Sex Ratio

 In education section, total literates in Thiruvananthapuram city are 645,863 of which 317,665 are males while 328,198 are females. Average literacy rate of Thiruvananthapuram city is 95.10 percent of which male and female literacy was 96.51 and 93.78 percent. The sex ratio of Thiruvananthapuram city is 1054 per 1000 males. Child sex ratio of girls is 967 per 1000 boys.   
  

### Thiruvananthapuram Slum Population

 Total no. of Slums in Thiruvananthapuram city & its Out Growth numbers 834 in which population of 3,320 resides. This is around 0.42% of total population of Thiruvananthapuram city & its outgrowth which is 788,271.

 Hinduism is majority [religion](https://www.census2011.co.in/census/city/462-thiruvananthapuram.html#) in Thiruvananthapuram city with 68.51 % followers. Christianity is second most popular religion in Thiruvananthapuram city with 16.79 % following it. In Thiruvananthapuram city, Islam is followed by 13.77 %, Jainism by 0.00 %, Sikhism by 0.02 % and Buddhism by 0.01 %. ##### City Profile

![Image 7: Image](https://smartcitytvm.in/images/Content_images/trv_map.jpg)

*   Thiruvananthapuram - Capital city of the Indian state of Kerala
*   Reffered by Mahatma Gandhi as the Évergreen city of India
*   Population - 9.86 lakh (2011 Census)
*   Growth Rate - 3.25% (2001 - 2011)
*   Area - 214.86sq.km
*   Population Density - 4,470 persons/sq.km
*   Work Participation Rate - 36%
*   Dominant Sectors - Tourism , IT, Education.

##### What makes Thiruvananthapuram Unique?

**Strength**

*   Major IT Hub in India
*   Natural Habitat and Rich cultural heritage
*   Ranked as city providing best quality of life
*   Ranked as best governed city in India

**Opportunities**

*   Prospects for strengthening of tourism economy
*   Upcoming metro rail projects and transhipment terminal
*   Electronic manufacturing based economic development

**Weakness**

*   Deficient Sewerage Infrastructure
*   Deteriorating condition of water bodies
*   Lack of end to end waste management system

**Threats**

*   Economic devaluation due to flooding and water logging in city core area
*   Environmental degradation
*   Motorized-vehicle oriented Urban Transport

*   Selected as ‘Best governed city in India’ in 2017 by Janaagraha Center for Citizenship & Democracy
*   Selected as ‘Best city’ of India under Housing & Transport category in 2013 by India Today.
*   Listed among top 10 cities in India on Vibrancy and Consumption Index by Morgon Stanley.
*   Rated as the ‘best 2nd tier metro’ with IT/ITeS infrastructure & second in terms of availability of human talent

# Thiruvananthapuram District - Population 2011-2026

An official Census 2011 detail of Thiruvananthapuram, a district of Kerala has been released by Directorate of Census Operations in Kerala. Enumeration of key persons was also done by census officials in Thiruvananthapuram District of Kerala.   
  
 In 2011, Thiruvananthapuram had population of 3,301,427 of which male and female were 1,581,678 and 1,719,749 respectively. In 2001 census, Thiruvananthapuram had a population of 3,234,356 of which males were 1,569,917 and remaining 1,664,439 were females. Thiruvananthapuram District population constituted 9.88 percent of total Maharashtra population. In 2001 census, this figure for Thiruvananthapuram District was at 10.16 percent of Maharashtra population.   
  
 There was change of 2.07 percent in the population compared to population as per 2001. In the previous census of India 2001, Thiruvananthapuram District recorded increase of 9.76 percent to its population compared to 1991.

Plan Trips

  

## Thiruvananthapuram Literacy Rate

Average literacy rate of Thiruvananthapuram in 2011 were 93.02 compared to 93.02 of 2001. If things are looked out at gender wise, male and female literacy were 95.06 and 91.17 respectively. For 2001 census, same figures stood at 92.64 and 86.14 in Thiruvananthapuram District. Total literate in Thiruvananthapuram District were 2,785,408 of which male and female were 1,354,857 and 1,430,551 respectively. In 2001, Thiruvananthapuram District had 2,558,494 in its district.

  

## Thiruvananthapuram Sex Ratio

With regards to Sex Ratio in Thiruvananthapuram, it stood at 1087 per 1000 male compared to 2001 census figure of 1060. The average national sex ratio in India is 940 as per latest reports of Census 2011 Directorate. In 2011 census, child sex ratio is 964 girls per 1000 boys compared to figure of 962 girls per 1000 boys of 2001 census data.

In census enumeration, data regarding child under 0-6 age were also collected for all districts including Thiruvananthapuram. There were total 307,061 children under age of 0-6 against 368,515 of 2001 census. Of total 307,061 male and female were 156,377 and 150,684 respectively. Child Sex Ratio as per census 2011 was 964 compared to 962 of census 2001. In 2011, Children under 0-6 formed 9.30 percent of Thiruvananthapuram District compared to 11.39 percent of 2001. There was net change of -2.09 percent in this compared to previous census of India.

Population statistics database

  

## Thiruvananthapuram Houseless Data

In 2011, total 359 families live on footpath or without any roof cover in Thiruvananthapuram district of Kerala. Total Population of all who lived without roof at the time of Census 2011 numbers to 775. This approx 0.023474697456585% of total population of Thiruvananthapuram district.

  

## Thiruvananthapuram District Density

The initial provisional data released by census India 2011, shows that density of Thiruvananthapuram district for 2011 is 1,508 people per sq. km. In 2001, Thiruvananthapuram district density was at 1,476 people per sq. km. Thiruvananthapuram district administers 2,189 square kilometers of areas.

  

### Thiruvananthapuram District Urban/Rural 2011

Out of the total Thiruvananthapuram population for 2011 census, 53.66 percent lives in urban regions of district. In total 1,771,596 people lives in urban areas of which males are 856,814 and females are 914,782. Sex Ratio in urban region of Thiruvananthapuram district is 1068 as per 2011 census data. Similarly child sex ratio in Thiruvananthapuram district was 962 in 2011 census. Child population (0-6) in urban region was 159,071 of which males and females were 81,077 and 77,994. This child population figure of Thiruvananthapuram district is 9.46 % of total urban population. Average literacy rate in Thiruvananthapuram district as per census 2011 is 94.14 % of which males and females are 95.91 % and 92.49 % literates respectively. In actual number 1,517,986 people are literate in urban region of which males and females are 744,001 and 773,985 respectively.   
  
 As per 2011 census, 46.34 % population of Thiruvananthapuram districts lives in rural areas of villages. The total Thiruvananthapuram district population living in rural areas is 1,529,831 of which males and females are 724,864 and 804,967 respectively. In rural areas of Thiruvananthapuram district, sex ratio is 1111 females per 1000 males. If child sex ratio data of Thiruvananthapuram district is considered, figure is 965 girls per 1000 boys. Child population in the age 0-6 is 147,990 in rural areas of which males were 75,300 and females were 72,690. The child population comprises 10.39 % of total rural population of Thiruvananthapuram district. Literacy rate in rural areas of Thiruvananthapuram district is 91.72 % as per census data 2011. Gender wise, male and female literacy stood at 94.04 and 89.66 percent respectively. In total, 1,267,422 people were literate of which males and females were 610,856 and 656,566 respectively.

# Thiruvananthapuram Urban Region Population 2011 - 2026

As per [data](https://www.census2011.co.in/census/metropolitan/421-thiruvananthapuram.html#) released by Govt. of India for Census 2011, Thiruvananthapuram is an Urban Agglomeration coming under category of Million Plus UA/City. [Thiruvananthapuram city](https://www.census2011.co.in/census/city/462-thiruvananthapuram.html "Thiruvananthapuram City Population") is governed by Municipal Corporation and is situated in Thiruvananthapuram Urban Region.   
  
 The total population of Thiruvananthapuram UA/Metropolitan region is 1,679,754. The male population of which is 813,065 while female population is 866,689.

Travel Guides & Travelogues

  
  

### Thiruvananthapuram Population 2026

 Population of Thiruvananthapuram city in 2026 is approximately 2,528,000. The last census was conducted in 2011 and the schedule census for Thiruvananthapuram Metropolitian region in 2021 was postponed due to Covid. The current estimates of Thiruvananthapuram urban area is based on past growth rate. Once govt conducts census for Thiruvananthapuram region, we will update the same on this page in 2026.   
  

### Thiruvananthapuram Literacy Rate

 The literacy rate of Thiruvananthapuram Agglomeration is 94.20% which is higher than National Urban average of 85 %. Literacy rate for male and female for Thiruvananthapuram stood at 95.96 % and 92.56 % respectively. Total literates in Thiruvananthapuram UA were 1,441,212 of which males were 706,963 and remaining 734,249 were females.   
  

### Thiruvananthapuram Child Population

 The children (0-6 age) population of Thiruvananthapuram UA is around 8.91 % of total Thiruvananthapuram UA population which is lower than National Urban average of 10.93 %. Total children in Thiruvananthapuram Urban region were 149,746 of which male were 76,323 while remaining 73,423 childs were female.   
  

### Thiruvananthapuram Sex Ratio

 The sex ratio of female to male in Thiruvananthapuram UA was found higher with figure of 1066 females against national urban average of 926 females per 1000 males. For children (0-6 age), girls were 962 per 1000 boys in Thiruvananthapuram Urban region against national average of 902 girls per 1000 boys.

# Kerala Population 2026 | Sex Ratio | Literacy

As per details from Census 2011, Kerala has population of 3.34 Crores, an increase from figure of 3.18 Crore in 2001 census. Total population of Kerala as per lastest census data is 33,406,061 of which male and female are 16,027,412 and 17,378,649 respectively. In 2001, total population was 31,841,374 in which males were 15,468,614 while females were 16,372,760. The total population growth in this decade was 4.91 percent while in previous decade it was 9.42 percent. The population of Kerala forms 2.76 percent of India in 2011. In 2001, the figure was 3.10 percent.

## Kerala Sex Ratio 2026

Sex Ratio in Kerala is 1084 i.e. for each 1000 male, which is below national average of 940 as per latest census. In 2001, the sex ratio of female was 1058 per 1000 males in Kerala.

## Kerala State Information

 Recently as per Kerala census data, 90.67% houses are owned while 7.31% were rented. In all, 68.45% couples in Kerala lived in single family. In 2011, 74.24% of Kerala population had access to Banking and Non-Banking Finance Corporation. Only 6.27% of Kerala population had internet facility which is likely to improve in 2021 due to Reliance Jio and Airtel. This is likely to see increased ecommerce penetration of Flipkart/Amazon in Kerala. 10.22% of family in Kerala owned car while 24.07% owned two wheller. Due to increase in literacy rate of Kerala, we are also seeing increase in interest in purchasing Health and Life Insurance policies by Kerala population. In few months we will also get details of election data for Kerala.   
  
**While Thiruvananthapuram is the capital city of Kerala state, largest remains Kochi as per census 2011.** The languages spoken in the Kerala state includes Malayalam and English. In total Kerala (KL) state comprises 14 districts. The ISOCODE assigned by International Organization for Standardization for Kerala state is KL.

##### Welcome to Smart City Thiruvananthapuram Ltd.

Smart City Thiruvananthapuram Limited is an Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) set up for implementation of Smart City Mission of Government of India with a project overlay of Rs. 1538 Cr. Thiruvananthapuram was selected in the third round of Smart City Selection and secured first rank in the Smart City Challenge in 2017.  
  

The proposal submitted to GOI had 43 projects aimed at improving basic infrastructure of the city and harnessing the use of IT based solutions to make the City Smart.  
  
The projects can be grouped into two categories; Pan City Solution (IT based solution) for entire corporation area and Area based development (ABD) Projects which are specifically targeted for 9 wards in the City Centre as a retrofit model.

The Census India body has reported on the census facts of Indian cities in 2011. Howbeit, the census survey is conducted on those cities only with a population value over 1 lakh. The census 2011 data of India covers information on all the chief yardsticks such as total population, literacy, child ratio etc. The article here aims to present the major Census Facts 2011 Cities.   
  
 When it comes to India population 2011 by city, it has been found that Greater Mumbai city contributes largely towards the population increment in the country. The census 2011 total population of India is 1.21 billion of which Mumbai of Maharashtra hosts 1.25 crores of population figures. The second most populated city in the country is Delhi with a population value of 11,007, 835.   
  
 On the contrary, Nagda city in Uttar Pradesh shows the least population value according to urban population census 2011. Nagda houses a population of 100,036. The Census India has also reported on the percentage of literacy rates in the city. As per the Census 2011 survey, Aizwal city in Mizoram shows the optimum rate of literacy in the country with 98.80% of literacy rate. It's closely followed by Kochi city of Kerala with a literacy rate of 97.49%. The Indian city with lowest literacy rate is Rampur. Rampur is situated in Uttar Pradesh and shows a literacy rate of 60.74%. Khurja city from the same state is the second least literate city in the country with a literacy rate of 67.63%.   
  
 In regards to sex ratio in the country, the Kozhikode city from the state of Kerala shows the optimum women sex ratio with 1093 females per 1000 men. When it comes to the lowest sex ratio in the Indian cities, two Gujarat cities have been found with minimal sex ratio among the cities surveyed. These two cities are Vapi with 734 females per 1,000 males and Surat with 754 females per 1,000 males.   
  
 When it comes to the number of children, Delhi shows the highest child figure (0-6 years) with a population of around 1,209,275 children in average. The second largest figure is found in Mumbai which hosts a child population of 1,139,146. The least number of children is found in the Darjeeling city of West Bengal. Darjeeling is a small city with a child population of 6,547 on an average. Then, city with second least child population is Khardah (West Bengal) with 6,579 numbers of children in average.

# District Census 2011

According to the Census Statistics 2011, the population of India was 1,210,854,977 with 623,270,258 males and 587,584,719 females. Literacy was found to be a total of 74.04% with 65.46% literate females and 82.14% males. This was a 9.81% increase since the last census. The density of population was found out to be 382 per square kilometers. The total sex ratio was 940 females to 1000 males. The child sex ratio (of ages 0 to 6 years old) was 914 females to 1000 males. The growth rate was 17.64% and the death rate was 21.5%.   
  
 Census is the process by which the information of a given population is calculated on the basis of economical, educational and social records, in a given period of time. Census is calculated after regular time intervals. These are some basic census facts. In India, the census is carried out every 5 years. The last census was calculated in the year 2011. This official census 2011 was the 15th census calculation which was done India. It was carried out in two main phases- population listing and house enumeration.

India is a vast territory with 28 states, 7 Union Territories, umpteen numbers of cities and several districts. India's official census 2011 reveals major census facts concerning all the major parameters in the society such as population, density, growth rate, literacy, sex ratio etc. Much like the states and cities, the Indian districts too come under the survey of the Indian Census body- India's census statistics 2011 reports details on 640 districts in the country from both the Union Territories and the Indian states. The census data were gathered from each of the district households. Here is a short brief highlighting the principle pointers of Census Facts 2011 Districts.   
  
 With regards to population, the Thane district of Maharashtra is found to be the optimum populated district in India with a population of around 1.11 crore. Interestingly, as per the urban population census 2011, Maharashtra houses the most populated city (Mumbai) of India as well. Thane is closely followed by North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal which hosts a population value of 10,082,852. The Dibang Valley District of Arunachal Pradesh shows the least population in the country with a population figure of 7,948. The second least populated district is from Arunachal Pradesh as well- Anjaw district with a population figure of 21,089.   
  
 According to India's district census 2011, the Serchhip district of Mizoram state is the optimum literate district in the country with 98.76% of literacy rate. It's closely followed by Mahe district in Puducherry with a literacy rate of 98.35%. The Koraput district in Orissa is the least literate district in the country with a literacy rate of 49.87%. The 2nd least literate district is Bharaich in Uttar Pradesh with a literacy rate of 51.10%.   
  
 The North East Delhi features the highest density/square kilometer of 37346 individuals. The Dibang Valley district in Arunachal Pradesh shows the least density/sq. km. With regard to the sex ratio in the Indian districts, Mahe district of Puducherry reveals the optimum sex ratio with 1176 females /1000 males. On the contrary, the Jhajjar district of Haryana shows the lowest sex ratio with 774 females to 1000 males. In population growth rate, the Kurung Kumey district of Arunachal Pradesh shows the highest growth rate in the country with figure of 111.01 %. On the other hand, the North & Middle Andaman district of Andaman & Nicobar Islands shows the lowest growth rate in the country: -0.07%.

# Thrissur Population 2026

Thrissur city is governed by Municipal Corporation which comes under [Thrissur Metropolitan Region](https://www.census2011.co.in/census/metropolitan/419-thrissur.html). The Thrissur city is located in Kerala state of India.

Travel Guides & Travelogues

  
 The current estimate population of Thrissur city in 2026 is 473,000 , while Thrissur metro population is estimated at 2,801,000 . # Kozhikode Population 2026

Kozhikode city is governed by Municipal Corporation which comes under [Kozhikode Metropolitan Region](https://www.census2011.co.in/census/metropolitan/418-kozhikode.html). The Kozhikode city is located in Kerala state of India.

City & Local Guides

  
 The current estimate population of Kozhikode city in 2026 is 647,000 , while Kozhikode metro population is estimated at 3,053,000 . The last census was conducted in 2011 and the schedule census for Kozhikode city in 2021 was postponed due to Covid. The current estimates of Kozhikode city are based on past growth rate. Once govt conducts census for Kozhikode city, we will update the same here in 2026. As per provisional reports of Census India, population of Kozhikode in 2011 is 431,560. Although Kozhikode city has population of 431,560; its urban / metropolitan population is 2,028,399. 
### Kozhikode Literacy Rate and Sex Ratio

 In education section, total literates in Kozhikode city are 375,027 of which 180,019 are males while 195,008 are females. Average literacy rate of Kozhikode city is 96.53 percent of which male and female literacy was 97.71 and 95.47 percent. The sex ratio of Kozhikode city is 1093 per 1000 males. Child sex ratio of girls is 965 per 1000 boys.   
  

### Kozhikode Slum Population

 Total no. of Slums in Kozhikode city & its Out Growth numbers 9,039 in which population of 50,343 resides. This is around 9.15% of total population of Kozhikode city & its outgrowth which is 550,440.   
  

### Kozhikode [Religion](https://www.census2011.co.in/census/city/456-kozhikode.html#)

 Hinduism is majority [religion](https://www.census2011.co.in/census/city/456-kozhikode.html#) in Kozhikode city with 57.37 % followers. Islam is second most popular religion in city of Kozhikode with approximately 37.66 % following it. In Kozhikode city, Christinity is followed by 4.60 %, Jainism by 0.09 %, Sikhism by 0.01 % and Buddhism by 0.01 %. # City Census 2011

The official census in India is calculated every 5 years. The most recent one was conducted in the year 2011. The entire process was done in 2 main phases of house listing and population listing respectively. The official census calculation started in the month of April, 2010. The town, district, village and city population 2011 was calculated over a period of 1 year. There are over 6lac villages and thousands of towns and districts in India.   
  
 The data was collected on the basis of several categories like age, sex, occupation, housing details, ownership details, literacy rates, standard of living and other details. There were certain criteria and definitions chalked out for the census of 2011. The total population of Urban Agglomeration (UA) and the city's population 2011 were calculated. The total census population of India 2011 was found out to be 1,210,854,977. Due to fast urbanization and developing and growing technology, it has been predicted that within 50 years, the population will go beyond one and a half billion.   
  
 Now, we need to know which places fell under the category of cities and UA category. All places which had a municipality, a corporation, notified town area community or a cantonment board was known to fall under the category of city or UA. Also these places were chosen under the category as all of them had a population over 5000 and more than 75% of the male population was found to be engaged in non-agricultural working sectors. The basic city population in India had seen a good amount of growth due to urbanization and raised literacy levels. It was calculated that in the year 2011, there are 4041 statutory towns, 3894 census towns, 475 UAs and 981 outgrowths from a number that was 3799 for statutory towns, 1362 for census towns, 384 UAs and 962 outgrowths. So there was an increase in every one of the places.   
  
 Here are the details of population about the major cities **(excluding Agglomeration)** . Mumbai - 12,442,373, Delhi - 11,034,555, Bangalore - 8,443,675, Hyderabad - 6,731,790, Ahmadabad - 5,577,940, Chennai - 4,646,732, Kolkata - 4,496,694, Surat - 4,467,797, Pune - 3,124,458, Jaipur - 3,046,163. Urbans areas surrounding Cities are combinely called Urban Agglomeration.   
  
 The City Populations 2011 clearly shows how important cities are in India and how fast India is developing. The urbanization factor and the educational factors are the most important factors which play a huge role in this kind of urban population density.

##### City Profile

![Image 7: Image](https://smartcitytvm.in/images/Content_images/trv_map.jpg)

*   Thiruvananthapuram - Capital city of the Indian state of Kerala
*   Reffered by Mahatma Gandhi as the Évergreen city of India
*   Population - 9.86 lakh (2011 Census)
*   Growth Rate - 3.25% (2001 - 2011)
*   Area - 214.86sq.km
*   Population Density - 4,470 persons/sq.km
*   Work Participation Rate - 36%
*   Dominant Sectors - Tourism , IT, Education.

##### What makes Thiruvananthapuram Unique?

**Strength**

*   Major IT Hub in India
*   Natural Habitat and Rich cultural heritage
*   Ranked as city providing best quality of life
*   Ranked as best governed city in India

**Opportunities**

*   Prospects for strengthening of tourism economy
*   Upcoming metro rail projects and transhipment terminal
*   Electronic manufacturing based economic development

**Weakness**

*   Deficient Sewerage Infrastructure
*   Deteriorating condition of water bodies
*   Lack of end to end waste management system

**Threats**

*   Economic devaluation due to flooding and water logging in city core area
*   Environmental degradation
*   Motorized-vehicle oriented Urban Transport

*   Selected as ‘Best governed city in India’ in 2017 by Janaagraha Center for Citizenship & Democracy
*   Selected as ‘Best city’ of India under Housing & Transport category in 2013 by India Today.
*   Listed among top 10 cities in India on Vibrancy and Consumption Index by Morgon Stanley.
*   Rated as the ‘best 2nd tier metro’ with IT/ITeS infrastructure & second in terms of availability of human talent

Thrissur city is governed by Municipal Corporation which comes under [Thrissur Metropolitan Region](https://www.census2011.co.in/census/metropolitan/419-thrissur.html). The Thrissur city is located in Kerala state of India.

Travel Guides & Travelogues

  
 The current estimate population of Thrissur city in 2026 is 473,000 , while Thrissur metro population is estimated at 2,801,000 . The last census was conducted in 2011 and the schedule census for Thrissur city in 2021 was postponed due to Covid. The current estimates of Thrissur city are based on past growth rate. Once govt conducts census for Thrissur city, we will update the same here in 2026. As per provisional reports of Census India, population of Thrissur in 2011 is 315,957. Although Thrissur city has population of 315,957; its urban / metropolitan population is 1,861,269.

### Thrissur Literacy Rate and Sex Ratio

 In education section, total literates in Thrissur city are 281,061 of which 136,148 are males while 144,913 are females. Average literacy rate of Thrissur city is 97.06 percent of which male and female literacy was 98.12 and 96.09 percent. The sex ratio of Thrissur city is 1075 per 1000 males. Child sex ratio of girls is 950 per 1000 boys.   
  

### Thrissur Slum Population

 Total no. of Slums in Thrissur city numbers 19,629 in which population of 79,801 resides. This is around 25.26% of total population of Thrissur city.

##### Welcome to Smart City Thiruvananthapuram Ltd.

Smart City Thiruvananthapuram Limited is an Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) set up for implementation of Smart City Mission of Government of India with a project overlay of Rs. 1538 Cr. Thiruvananthapuram was selected in the third round of Smart City Selection and secured first rank in the Smart City Challenge in 2017.  
  

The proposal submitted to GOI had 43 projects aimed at improving basic infrastructure of the city and harnessing the use of IT based solutions to make the City Smart.  
  
The projects can be grouped into two categories; Pan City Solution (IT based solution) for entire corporation area and Area based development (ABD) Projects which are specifically targeted for 9 wards in the City Centre as a retrofit model.

**Thiruvananthapuram Central Assembly constituency** is one of the 140 [state legislative assembly](link_5) constituencies in [Kerala](link_4), India. It is one of the seven assembly segments that constitute the [Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha constituency").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(State_Assembly_constituency)#cite_note-1)

Thiruvananthapuram Assembly constituency was established by the 2008 delimitation. Before, it was known as Trivandrum West Assembly Constituency from 1977 to 2008, and Trivandrum-I Assembly constituency from 1957 to 1977.

## Local self-governed segments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_Assembly_constituency&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Local self-governed segments")]

## The internet we were promised.

[[edit](https://donate.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:Appeal/default/en&action=edit&section=T-1 "Edit section: The internet we were promised.")]

Thank you for considering a donation to the Wikimedia Foundation.

We invite you to reflect on the number of times you visited Wikipedia in the last year. If the knowledge you gained here was valuable, please join the 2% of readers who donate. Any amount helps: $5, $20, $50, or whatever feels right to you today.

The internet we were promised—a place of free, collaborative, and accessible knowledge—is under constant threat. On Wikipedia, volunteers work together to create and verify the pages you rely on, supported by tools that undo vandalism within minutes, ensuring the information you seek is trustworthy.

If Wikipedia has given you useful knowledge this year, please give back. There are no small contributions: every edit counts, every donation counts.

Thank you.

## Where your donation goes

[[edit](https://donate.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:Infobox/Default/en&action=edit&section=T-1 "Edit section: Where your donation goes")]

**Technology**: Servers, bandwidth, maintenance, development. Wikipedia is one of the top 10 websites in the world, and it runs on a fraction of what other top websites spend.

**People and Projects**: The other top websites have thousands of employees. Wikimedia Foundation has about 700 staff and contractors to support a wide variety of projects, making your donation a great investment in a highly-efficient not-for-profit organization.

[Tax deductibility information](https://wikimediafoundation.org/give/donor-frequently-asked-questions/#tax-deductibility)

We do not sell or trade your information to anyone. By donating, you agree to share your personal information with the Wikimedia Foundation, the nonprofit organization that hosts Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects, and its service providers pursuant to our [donor policy](https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:LandingCheck?landing_page=Donor_privacy_policy&basic=true&language=en). Wikimedia Foundation and its service providers are located in the United States and in other countries whose privacy laws may not be equivalent to your own. For more information please read our [donor policy](https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:LandingCheck?landing_page=Donor_privacy_policy&basic=true&language=en).

Monthly donations will be debited on the same date each month as your first gift, until canceled. Donations made on the 29th, 30th, or 31st will be charged on the last day of shorter months. Yearly recurring donations will be debited on the anniversary of the first gift. For questions, please contact donate@wikimedia.org.

**Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation** is the [municipal corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation_(India) "Municipal corporation (India)") that administrates the city of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"), the capital of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). The city corporation is spread over 214.86 km 2 with 101 wards and a population of 957,730 inhabitants.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation#cite_note-5) It includes the [Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly") constituencies of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Assembly_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Assembly constituency"), [Vattiyoorkavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattiyoorkavu_Assembly_constituency "Vattiyoorkavu Assembly constituency"), [Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency "Nemom Assembly constituency"), [Kazhakkoottam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakootam_Assembly_constituency "Kazhakootam Assembly constituency") and four wards of the [Kovalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kovalam_Assembly_constituency "Kovalam Assembly constituency") constituency.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The Conservancy Department was started in Thiruvananthapuram in 1877 during the reign of the king [Ayilyam Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayilyam_Thirunal "Ayilyam Thirunal") of the [Travancore kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). Under this arrangement, the town was divided into 5 divisions, namely Kottaykkakam ([areas inside the Fort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Fort "East Fort")), [Chalai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalai,_Thiruvananthapuram "Chalai, Thiruvananthapuram"), Sreevaraham, [Manacaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manacaud "Manacaud") and [Pettah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pettah,_Thiruvananthapuram "Pettah, Thiruvananthapuram").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation#cite_note-6)

The first president of the Committee was Dewan Peshkar Iraviperur Pillai. There were 19 members in the committee. The Thiruvananthapuram Municipality came into existence in 1920. After two decades, during the reign of [Sree Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chithira_Thirunal_Balarama_Varma "Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma"), Thiruvananthapuram Municipality was converted into Municipal Corporation on 30 October 1940.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation#cite_note-7)

**Pannian Ravindran** (born 22 December 1945) is an Indian[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannyan_Raveendran#cite_note-1) politician from [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") and former state secretary of Kerala State Committee of [CPI (Communist Party of India)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India "Communist Party of India") from 2012 to 2015. He was a [member](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament,_Lok_Sabha "Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha") of the [14th Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/14th_Lok_Sabha "14th Lok Sabha") of India and represented the [Thiruvananthapuram constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Thiruvananthapuram (Lok Sabha constituency)").

## Early Life & Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pannian_Ravindran&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early Life & Education")]

Ravindran lived in a thatched house with mud walls as a child, his family was politically involved with the [CPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India "Communist Party of India").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannyan_Raveendran#cite_note-:0-2) His father died when he was 12 and due to poverty, he stopped going to school and started working at a [beedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beedi "Beedi") factory in [Kakkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kakkad,_Kannur "Kakkad, Kannur") in order to support his family. His weekly wage was 50 [paise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paise "Paise").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannyan_Raveendran#cite_note-:0-2) Therefore his education is a 5th pass.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannyan_Raveendran#cite_note-3)

## From today's featured article

[![Image 4: Pennsylvania State Capitol](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_%2850035197647%29.jpg/250px-Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_%2850035197647%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_(50035197647).jpg "Pennsylvania State Capitol")

The **[Pennsylvania State Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_State_Capitol "Pennsylvania State Capitol")** is located in [Harrisburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrisburg,_Pennsylvania "Harrisburg, Pennsylvania"). The building was designed by [Joseph Miller Huston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Miller_Huston "Joseph Miller Huston") and completed in 1906 in a [Beaux-Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaux-Arts_architecture "Beaux-Arts architecture") style with decorative [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_Revival_architecture "Renaissance Revival architecture") themes. It houses the legislative chambers for the [Pennsylvania General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_General_Assembly "Pennsylvania General Assembly"), the Harrisburg chambers for the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Pennsylvania "Supreme Court of Pennsylvania") and [Superior Court of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superior_Court_of_Pennsylvania "Superior Court of Pennsylvania"), and the offices of [the state's governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_Pennsylvania "List of governors of Pennsylvania") and [lieutenant governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_Pennsylvania "Lieutenant Governor of Pennsylvania"). The capitol project was the subject of a [graft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graft_(politics) "Graft (politics)") scandal, as the construction and furnishing cost three times more than the General Assembly had appropriated for the project. The Pennsylvania State Capitol is often referred to as a "palace of art" because of its many sculptures, murals, and stained-glass windows, most of which are Pennsylvania-themed or were made in Pennsylvania. The building was listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") in 1977 and designated a [National Historic Landmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Historic_Landmark "National Historic Landmark") in 2006. _(**[Full article...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania\_State\_Capitol "Pennsylvania State Capitol")**)_

*   ... that **[Grady Prestage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grady_Prestage "Grady Prestage")** was the first African American elected to the [Fort Bend County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Bend_County,_Texas "Fort Bend County, Texas") commissioners' court since Reconstruction?
*   ... that John James Audubon gave his wife ownership of **[his Manhattan estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audubon_Park,_Manhattan "Audubon Park, Manhattan")** to prevent debt collectors from seizing it?

**[Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") Parliamentary (Lok Sabha) Constituency** is one of the 20 parliamentary constituencies in Kerala, India. It is located in [Thiruvananthapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district") and encompasses the major part of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") city, the capital of [Kerala State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").

The incumbent MP of this constituency, [Shashi Tharoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor "Shashi Tharoor") of the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"), has been elected on 4 consecutive occasions: 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024. He is the longest serving Member of Parliament to have represented the constituency.

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

This constituency is dominated By [Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") and [Nadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-2) As per the electoral roll for the 2024 polls, the total electorate is of 14,03,281 people including 7,27,469 women, 6,75,771 men and 41 transgender people.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-3) Out of total electorate, 26% is rural and 74% is urban. The Scheduled castes (SC) and Scheduled tribes (ST) is 9.82% and 0.45%, respectively of total electorate.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-4) The constituency also has highest proportion of [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") and [Converted Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_to_Christianity "Conversion to Christianity") in Kerala.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-5)[Nairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") dominates the urban segments of [Kazhakootam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakootam_Assembly_constituency "Kazhakootam Assembly constituency"),[Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency "Nemom Assembly constituency"),[Vattiyoorkavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattiyoorkavu_Assembly_constituency "Vattiyoorkavu Assembly constituency") and [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Assembly_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Assembly constituency") While the [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") are Concentrated on [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara_Assembly_constituency "Neyyattinkara Assembly constituency"),[Parassala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parassala_Assembly_constituency "Parassala Assembly constituency"),[Kovalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kovalam_Assembly_constituency "Kovalam Assembly constituency").

As per the voter list published by the Election commission for the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, there were 13,34,665 voters in the electorate and 1077 polling stations in this constituency.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-ceo.kerala.gov.in-6) The voter turnout for the 2019 Lok Sabha election was 73.45% where as it was 68.63% and 65.74% in the 2014 and 2009 elections respectively.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)#cite_note-7)

**Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation** is the [municipal corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation_(India) "Municipal corporation (India)") that administrates the city of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"), the capital of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). The city corporation is spread over 214.86 km 2 with 101 wards and a population of 957,730 inhabitants.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation#cite_note-5) It includes the [Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Legislative_Assembly "Kerala Legislative Assembly") constituencies of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Assembly_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Assembly constituency"), [Vattiyoorkavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattiyoorkavu_Assembly_constituency "Vattiyoorkavu Assembly constituency"), [Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency "Nemom Assembly constituency"), [Kazhakkoottam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakootam_Assembly_constituency "Kazhakootam Assembly constituency") and four wards of the [Kovalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kovalam_Assembly_constituency "Kovalam Assembly constituency") constituency.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The Conservancy Department was started in Thiruvananthapuram in 1877 during the reign of the king [Ayilyam Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayilyam_Thirunal "Ayilyam Thirunal") of the [Travancore kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). Under this arrangement, the town was divided into 5 divisions, namely Kottaykkakam ([areas inside the Fort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Fort "East Fort")), [Chalai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalai,_Thiruvananthapuram "Chalai, Thiruvananthapuram"), Sreevaraham, [Manacaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manacaud "Manacaud") and [Pettah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pettah,_Thiruvananthapuram "Pettah, Thiruvananthapuram").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation#cite_note-6)

The first president of the Committee was Dewan Peshkar Iraviperur Pillai. There were 19 members in the committee. The Thiruvananthapuram Municipality came into existence in 1920. After two decades, during the reign of [Sree Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chithira_Thirunal_Balarama_Varma "Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma"), Thiruvananthapuram Municipality was converted into Municipal Corporation on 30 October 1940.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation#cite_note-7)

## Administration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Administration")]

The city corporation is governed by a council of 101 members, headed by the [Mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor "Mayor"). The members of the Council are elected every five years, with the latest election having been in 2025. It constitutes Standing Committees for exercising its powers, discharging such duties or performing such functions as are provided for in the [Kerala Municipalities Act.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_governance_in_India "Municipal governance in India")

The Mayor is elected by the councilors from among themselves. They chair Council meetings and are responsible for the overall supervision and control of the administrative functions of the Municipal Corporation.

The Deputy Mayor is the Chairman of the Finance Standing Committee and also presides over the Council meetings during the absence of the Mayor. The Secretary of the TMC is a civil servant appointed by the Kerala Government. The law and order of the city is handled by the [Thiruvananthapuram City Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_City_Police "Thiruvananthapuram City Police") Commissioner. The total police strength in the city including the Armed Reserve camp at Nandavanam and the SAP camp at Peroorkada, is about 4,500.

The corporation was originally (in 1940) divided into 24 wards, covering an area of 30.66 km 2. Through the years, the city corporation has grown to 101 wards, and now the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation Council is the second largest democratically elected body in Kerala after the Legislative Assembly.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Corporation#cite_note-8)

**[Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") Parliamentary (Lok Sabha) Constituency** is one of the 20 parliamentary constituencies in Kerala, India. It is located in [Thiruvananthapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district") and encompasses the major part of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") city, the capital of [Kerala State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").

The incumbent MP of this constituency, [Shashi Tharoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor "Shashi Tharoor") of the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"), has been elected on 4 consecutive occasions: 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024. He is the longest serving Member of Parliament to have represented the constituency.

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

This constituency is dominated By [Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") and [Nadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-2) As per the electoral roll for the 2024 polls, the total electorate is of 14,03,281 people including 7,27,469 women, 6,75,771 men and 41 transgender people.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-3) Out of total electorate, 26% is rural and 74% is urban. The Scheduled castes (SC) and Scheduled tribes (ST) is 9.82% and 0.45%, respectively of total electorate.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-4) The constituency also has highest proportion of [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") and [Converted Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_to_Christianity "Conversion to Christianity") in Kerala.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-5)[Nairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") dominates the urban segments of [Kazhakootam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakootam_Assembly_constituency "Kazhakootam Assembly constituency"),[Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency "Nemom Assembly constituency"),[Vattiyoorkavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattiyoorkavu_Assembly_constituency "Vattiyoorkavu Assembly constituency") and [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Assembly_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Assembly constituency") While the [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") are Concentrated on [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara_Assembly_constituency "Neyyattinkara Assembly constituency"),[Parassala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parassala_Assembly_constituency "Parassala Assembly constituency"),[Kovalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kovalam_Assembly_constituency "Kovalam Assembly constituency").

As per the voter list published by the Election commission for the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, there were 13,34,665 voters in the electorate and 1077 polling stations in this constituency.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-ceo.kerala.gov.in-6) The voter turnout for the 2019 Lok Sabha election was 73.45% where as it was 68.63% and 65.74% in the 2014 and 2009 elections respectively.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-7)

* * *

##### A reknowned palace in Kerala, renowned as the birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma, showcasing traditional Kerala architecture, a preserved art studio, and a legacy of cultural and artistic significance.

Kilimanoor Palace, located in the Kilimanoor village of Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala, is a historic and culturally significant landmark. This sprawling complex, with its traditional Kerala architecture, lush surroundings, and rich history, offers visitors a fascinating glimpse into the royal heritage of Kerala. The palace is particularly renowned as the birthplace of the celebrated Indian painter Raja Ravi Varma, making it an essential destination for art lovers, history enthusiasts, and tourists.  
  
**Historical Significance**  
Kilimanoor Palace has a history that spans several centuries, dating back to the early 18th century. The palace was originally built by the royal family of Travancore as a residential and administrative center. Over the years, it has been the site of significant historical events and has hosted many distinguished guests, including British officials and Indian royalty. The most notable historical figure associated with Kilimanoor Palace is Raja Ravi Varma, one of India's greatest painters. Born in 1848, Ravi Varma is celebrated for his pioneering work in Indian art, blending traditional Indian themes with European techniques. The palace remains a symbol of his artistic legacy and continues to attract art aficionados from around the world.  
  
**Architectural Features**  
Kilimanoor Palace is an exemplar of traditional Kerala architecture, featuring wide verandahs, spacious courtyards, and long corridors. The palace's red-tiled roofs and brilliant white walls add to its picturesque charm. The architectural design incorporates local materials like wood and laterite stone, reflecting the indigenous construction techniques of the time.  
  
**Raja Ravi Varma Studio**  
The Chitrashala studio, designed by Raja Ravi Varma and built around 1875, is a significant part of Kilimanoor Palace. The studio boasts large glass windows that flood the space with natural light, creating an ideal environment for painting. It houses a dusty, aged easel and other tools used by Varma. The serene and inspiring surroundings include views of the flowering garden and paddy fields, which influenced Varma's works.  
  
**Cultural and Artistic Significance**  
Kilimanoor Palace is not only a historical site but also a cultural hub that celebrates the artistic heritage of Kerala. The palace's association with Raja Ravi Varma adds immense cultural value, as his works played a crucial role in shaping modern Indian art. Varma's paintings are renowned for their depictions of Hindu mythology, portraits of Indian women, and use of vibrant colors and intricate details. The palace preserves his memory with prints of his famous paintings, photographs, and personal artifacts. The Kilimanoor Palace Trust continues to uphold Varma's legacy by maintaining the palace and organizing events to celebrate his contributions to art. The palace regularly hosts art exhibitions, cultural programs, and workshops, promoting the arts and preserving the legacy of Raja Ravi Varma. Visitors can explore the museum dedicated to his works, attend lectures on his contributions to art, and participate in activities that highlight the rich cultural heritage of Kerala.  
  
**Accommodation**  
There are several accommodation options available in and around Kilimanoor, ranging from budget lodgings to luxury resorts. Many of these establishments offer comfortable stays with modern amenities, providing a convenient base for exploring Kilimanoor Palace and the surrounding attractions.  
  
**Visitor Information**  
The best time to visit Kilimanoor Palace is year-round, as its indoor setting ensures that weather conditions do not impact the experience, making it ideal for sightseeing and exploring the palace at any time.  
  
Hiring a local guide can enhance the visitor experience by providing detailed information about the historical and cultural significance of the palace. Guides can also offer insights into the life and works of Raja Ravi Varma and the architectural features of the complex.  
  
Kilimanoor Palace, with its historical significance, architectural splendor, and cultural heritage, offers a unique and enriching experience for visitors. Whether you are an art enthusiast, a history buff, or a curious traveler, the palace provides a fascinating glimpse into the royal legacy and artistic traditions of Kerala. A visit to Kilimanoor Palace is not only an educational journey but also an opportunity to connect with the timeless beauty and cultural richness of Kerala's past.

**Kilimanoor Palace** is a palace located in [Kilimanoor](link_0), in the Indian state of [Kerala](link_3).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_Palace#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_Palace#cite_note-2) It is the birthplace of painter [Raja Ravi Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma "Raja Ravi Varma") and Raghava Varma, the father of king [Marthanda Varma](link_8).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_Palace#cite_note-Thrippadidaanam-3)

## The Palace

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kilimanoor_Palace&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: The Palace")]

The Palace complex covers more than six hectares, and comprises the traditional residential structures of Kerala, like the Nalukettu, small and medium-sized buildings, three ponds, wells and sacred groves (_kaavu_).

Raja Ravi Varma is said to have built and maintained some of the buildings from the proceeds of his paintings. Families related to the Travancore royal house continue to live here.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kilimanoor_Palace&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

The royal house at Choottayil, [Kilimanoor](link_0) has a history stretching back more than 300 years, although the oldest buildings are from a much earlier period.

### Association with the Travancore royal house

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kilimanoor_Palace&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Association with the Travancore royal house")]

In 1705, the son and two daughters of Ittammar Raja of [Beypore](link_9) Thattarikovilakam, the northern branch of [Parappanad](link_10) royal house, were adopted into the royal house of [Venad](link_11). The Ittammar Raja's sister and her sons, Rama Varma and Raghava Varma, settled in Kilimanoor and married the now-adopted sisters.

The lands around the present-day palace were a part of an estate which originally belonged to a [Pillai](link_12) ruling chief. The estate comprised several villages and was handed over to the family of Raghava Varma.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_Palace#cite_note-4)[Maharaja Marthanda Varma](link_8), the founder of the [Kingdom of Travancore](link_7), was the son of Raghava Varma.

In 1739, after Marthanda Varma ascended the throne, an alliance led by the [Dutch](link_13) Captain Hockert, was formed between [Kochi](link_13), [Thekkumkoor](link_14), [Desinganadu](link_15) and [Purakkad](link_16), due to their shared enmity towards Marthanda Varma. In 1740, this [allied force attacked Venad](link_17) and an army from Kilimanoor resisted and subsequently defeated them in the [Battle of Colachel](link_18). Although a small victory, this was the first time an Indian army had defeated a European power.

In 1753, in recognition of this feat, Marthanda Varma exempted the areas controlled by the Kilimanoor Palace, as well as most of the area under the present Kilimanoor and [Pazhayakunnummel](link_19) panchayats from taxes, and granted them autonomous status. Although the estate had been under his rule earlier, the present palace complex was built in 1753, together with the Ayyappa temple. The original temple was at Nerumkaithakotta, near Kozhikode for the family deity, Sastha or Ayyapan.

In the early 19th century, [Velu Thampi Dalawa](link_20) held meetings at Kilimanoor Palace while planning uprisings against the British. In 1809, he handed over his sword at the Palace before going into his final battle against the British. India's first President, [Dr Rajendra Prasad](link_21) received this sword from the palace and it was kept in the [National Museum](link_22) in [Delhi](link_23). Afterwards the sword was moved to the [Napier Museum](link_24) in Thiruvananthapuram.
